title: Audit Fly volume dvc-cache: what it stores, what's evictable, and whether 4GB is enough
description: Both Fly demo volumes (vol_vx2odmdqx7k9m3wr, vol_vdm7gedke5mew13v — 4GB each) are nearly full from /app/audio_volume/dvc-cache. As of 2026-04-30: machine 4d8930e0b00078 reports 3.9G used / 0 avail (100%), machine 56835012a60e68 reports 3.7G used / 88M avail (98%). The next deploy that needs to write to the volume will fail, and feedback.jsonl / pageviews.jsonl have nowhere to grow. The webapp depends on dvc-cache for audio playback — the staged demo MP3s under data/runs/<run>/audio/podcast*.mp3 are symlinks rewritten from /Volumes/Crucial X9/bleakhouse_audio to /app/audio_volume during stage_demo.sh, so the cache content backing those symlinks is load-bearing. We need to understand: (1) total cache size and per-file inventory, (2) which cache entries are referenced by symlinks under data/runs and which are orphaned, (3) whether expand-volume vs cache-eviction vs both is the right call, (4) whether the eager admin upload-blob route (/api/_admin/upload-blob, app.py:760) is still in use or has been retired by the dolt/staging path.
acceptance_criteria: (a) inventory script that lists every dvc-cache md5 and tags it referenced/orphaned by walking demo_data symlinks; (b) decision recorded in a bd decision: keep+expand, prune+keep4GB, or migrate dvc-cache off-volume; (c) if pruning, a rm-orphans script that runs as part of deploy_demo.sh.
notes:
Audit complete on 2026-04-30 (both Fly machines).

FINDINGS:
- Machine 4d8930e0b00078: 38 audio symlinks under /app/data/runs/*/audio/
  point at 38 distinct dvc-cache blobs. Cache contains exactly those 38
  blobs. 0 orphans, 0 missing.
- Machine 56835012a60e68: same 38-blob working set, plus 2 macOS
  AppleDouble files (_._06cb2eed..._ and _._21fb03cc..._) at 163 bytes
  each = 326 bytes of true orphan. Trivial.
- Cache size: 3.79 GB total, avg 99.7 MB per file, range 60-142 MB.
  Consistent with full-length podcast renders at typical mp3 bitrates.
  Nothing fits the 'orphan' profile (cache entry no current run links to).

CONCLUSION: The cache is not bloated. The 4GB Fly volumes are full
because the demo's working set is 3.8 GB and the volume is sized at
4 GB with zero headroom. Pruning won't help — there's nothing to prune.

USER HYPOTHESIS DISPROVED: expectation was that dvc-cache had more
than the webapp needs. It has exactly what the webapp needs, plus
326 bytes of macOS metadata.

DECISION SPACE FOR HEADROOM:
1. fly volumes extend to 8GB on each machine (cheapest, ~$0.30/mo extra)
2. Re-render at lower mp3 bitrate to halve file sizes (workshop-grade
   audio quality acceptable for demo? requires re-running TTS)
3. Trim demo to fewer podcasts (loses comparison breadth)
4. Move audio off the volume to S3/R2/Tigris (architectural change)

Recommendation: option 1 (extend volume). Lowest risk, lowest effort,
preserves all comparison cells. Decision can be recorded via bd decision
once user confirms.
close_reason: Audit complete + extended both Fly volumes 4GB→32GB. Cache contained exactly the 38 referenced blobs (no orphans). Volume now reports 32GB / 27GB free per machine. Cost: ~$9.60/mo total ($0.15/GB/mo × 64 GB).

title: Subtask: SQL view layer for matrix rows
description:
Design the SELECT queries that produce the matrix shape ('rows' of (novel, pipeline, panel, hostprep, generator, ref_tools) cells). For each cell, join the episode row to:
  - most recent script_version (by created_at)
  - most recent hostprep_version (if hostprep=1)
  - most recent audio_artifact (if any)
  - latest evaluation (if any)

Output one row per matrix axis tuple, with all the data the JS card renderer needs (status, has_audio, has_episode, has_reading_list, audio engine, etc).

Retrofits surface naturally because they're additional script_version / hostprep_version rows on the same episode — 'most recent' picks them up.

Define the queries as Python functions that return list[dict]. Don't call from any endpoint yet — just provide the building blocks.

Definition of done: 'matrix_rows()' returns rows that match what '_build_cached_snapshot()' currently produces, on a corpus where both can be compared.

title: Subtask: DVC stage that keeps experiments.db current
description:
Add a DVC stage 'expdb_scan' that runs 'uv run python -m enrichment.expdb scan --runs-dir data/runs' and produces 'data/experiments.db' as its output. Deps should be wide enough that any run-dir change retriggers it (probably 'data/runs' as a directory dep or a glob over per-run manifests).

title: Epic: Clean tracker built on a read-only experiment-DB view
description:
The webapp's matrix tracker currently discovers runs by scanning the filesystem and matching dir names against fixed (novel × pipeline × panel × hostprep × generator) tuples. This drifts: retrofit dirs (named '<canonical>_retrofit_<TS>') don't surface, audio-less runs are filtered out, audio variants and ref_tools are inferred from filename heuristics rather than data, and patching the discovery logic to fix one symptom keeps reintroducing the next.

Replace the whole stack with a clean rebuild:
  1. Source of truth is data/experiments.db (the existing SQLite ledger from BleakHouse-f6a). The DB is regenerable from data/runs via 'uv run python -m enrichment.expdb scan'.
  2. Webapp opens the DB read-only and queries it for matrix views. No filesystem walk, no dir-name regex.
  3. Each matrix cell is one episode row joined to its most-recent script_version + audio_artifact (if any), with retrofits naturally surfacing as fresher rows on the same (novel, panel, pipeline, hostprep, generator, ref_tools) coordinate.

Why now:
  - The 13-novel correct-by-construction retrofit batch produced runs that don't show in the matrix because they have retrofit-suffixed dir names. We want them to surface, alongside any future retrofits, without per-feature webapp patches.
  - The expdb schema already models exactly the axes the matrix wants — episode.UNIQUE(novel, panel, pipeline, hostprep, generator, ref_tools) is the matrix coordinate.
  - Filesystem discovery has been progressively patched throughout the webapp; the patches are accreting (synthesis filter, version parsing, retrofit lookup, audio variant detection). A clean rebuild is cheaper than another round of patching.

Out of scope for this epic (separate concerns):
  - Listener-facing accessibility/jargon work — covered by BleakHouse-5sq epic.
  - chat-ui — covered by BleakHouse-fi5 and its building blocks.

To be broken down into subtasks. Likely shape:
  - DB scan as a DVC stage so it stays current; webapp triggers a refresh on file change.
  - SQL view layer that produces matrix rows + cell details directly.
  - Read-only sqlite connection helper for the webapp.
  - Replacement /tracker/data endpoint backed by the view layer.
  - Retire _build_cached_snapshot, _discover_runs, _summarize_run_dir, _classify_run, RunIndexCache.
  - Migrate other webapp endpoints (/api/runs/<id>/prep, /tracker/versions, etc.) onto the same DB view layer.
  - Ensure deploy_demo.sh runs the DB scan + bundles the DB into the container.

Reference: BleakHouse-f6a (Experiments DB feature, P2, open) defines the ledger this epic consumes.
close_reason: Webapp tracker rebuilt on read-only experiments.db view: matrix, versions, novels, all-runs, prep all DB-backed; ~290 lines of FS-discovery code retired; deploy bundles DB into container. Live and verified.

title: B: run_manifest as the single source of truth (webapp/DVC architecture)
description: See docs/webapp_dvc_architecture.md for the full rationale. The webapp currently discovers artefacts by filesystem convention (podcast*.mp3, manifest_*.json patterns) while DVC owns the authoritative graph. The two views drift; the synthesis bug was one symptom. Build a per-run run_manifest.json produced by a new DVC stage that reads dvc.lock + filesystem and writes a single authoritative summary (axes, per-stage hash + fresh flag, audio_variants list with engines, dvc_lock_sha for cross-checking). Webapp reads run_manifest only; filesystem-convention discovery is removed in stages. Migration is 5 incremental steps (each leaves app working): (1) scripts/generate_run_manifest.py for one run (idempotent, manual). (2) DVC stage run_manifest@<id> with foreach over runs_by_id and deps on every upstream phase output. (3) webapp _load_run_manifest() reader; new code paths use it, old paths keep working. (4) migrate _available_versions, _summarize_run_dir, _discover_runs one at a time. (5) drop filesystem-convention paths. ~half a day in a focused session. Subsumes Tier 1 of the synthesis fix and makes Tier 2 (synthesis filter + cell badges) trivial. The architecturally important piece — transparency, maintainability, reproducibility all derive from this.
close_reason: Superseded by the new clean-tracker epic — webapp will be rebuilt around a read-only experiment-DB view rather than patched piecemeal. Reopen if any specific scope here turns out to belong outside the rebuild.

title: Embedding query augmentation experiments (C1 keyword, C3 graduated)
description:
Test whether augmenting embedding retrieval queries with demand-derived text produces predictable passage shifts comparable to transport's demand vector manipulation.

C1 (keyword augmentation): Append dimension keywords weighted by demand strength to each expert's retrieval queries. Use existing DIMENSION_DESCRIPTIONS from embedding_podcast.py. E.g. Blackstone demand social_critique=6 → append 'Focus on: social criticism, class, poverty (strong).'

C3 (graduated prompt prefix): Prepend demand-strength sentences that scale with the weight. demand=6 → 'Prioritise passages with strong social critique.' demand=1 → 'Note any atmospheric details.' demand=0 → nothing.

For each augmentation method:
1. Run 4-6 BH embedding variants with different expert demand profiles (matching the transport v01/v10/v11/v12/v19 configs)
2. Compute passage Jaccard vs baseline for each
3. Compare predictability (demand distance vs Jaccard correlation) against transport results from BleakHouse-it7

The claim to test: natural-language query steering is less predictable than numerical demand-vector steering.

title: Epic: Quantify transport manipulability
description:
Measure predictability of passage selection changes in response to demand manipulations. Three sub-tasks:

1. EXPERT SENSITIVITY (data exists): Analyse the 20 BH panel configs. For each pair, compute demand-vector distance vs passage Jaccard. Show that passage change is proportional to demand change. Plot demand distance vs Jaccard.

3. EMBEDDING COMPARISON: Show that the embedding pipeline has no equivalent manipulation lever. The same demand change that shifts 30% of transport passages has zero effect on embedding output (because embedding doesn't use demand profiles). This is the manipulability gap.

The claim: transport is manipulable (demand changes predict passage changes), embedding is not.

title: OpenAI gpt-5-mini enrichment coverage gap — fix selectivity/truncation in long chapters
description:
Stage 2 of OpenAI execution plan (BleakHouse-2nw3) produced enrichments for only 80% of paragraphs vs the Anthropic Haiku baseline. 21 of 69 chapters under-covered; worst is c21 (168 paragraphs in baseline, 14 in OpenAI output). Pattern: contiguous prefix truncation, not selective skipping. Not budget-bound — output_tokens avg 14k vs 50k cap. Hypothesis: reasoning.effort=minimal + json_schema strict permits short syntactically-valid `enrichments` lists.

Path options:
  A. Re-submit the 21 affected chapters with reasoning.effort=low. Cheapest test of the hypothesis.
  B. Add a minItems constraint to enrichments per-request based on observed paragraph count (requires per-request schemas — modify enrichment/submit_passages_enriched_openai.py to build a per-chunk schema with minItems = len(chunk)).
  C. Escalate the heavy chapters to gpt-5.4 for guaranteed coverage; gpt-5-mini for the rest.

Acceptance: paragraph coverage parity with the Anthropic baseline (within ±1%) for Bleak House.

Affected chapters (anth, oai): c12(117,15) c16(74,62) c17(128,19) c20(126,125) c21(168,14) c22(139,32) c23(162,110) c24(156,45) c26(138,19) c3(165,130) c33(?,?) c34(?,?) c54(161,51) — full list in BleakHouse-2nw3 notes.
notes:
2026-05-15: Implemented chunker fix in enrichment/submit_passages_enriched_openai.py.
- New DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE = 40 paragraphs, configurable via --chunk-size.
- Replaced the binary-split-only logic with uniform fixed-size chunking.
- For Bleak House (6,916 paragraphs across 69 chapters), this expands the batch from
  69 → 209 requests; worst-case chapter (c21, 168 paragraphs) becomes 5 chunks of ≤40.
- collect_passages_enriched_openai.py needs no changes — it already merges results by
  (chapter_id, paragraph_index) so multiple -partN responses per chapter just contribute
  disjoint paragraph indices.
- Cost impact: batch grows ~3x in request count but the work is the same; estimated
  rerun cost ~$1.10-1.50 (input slightly higher due to per-request system prompt overhead;
  output unchanged).

Next: resubmit Bleak House at chunk_size=40 and verify coverage parity with the Anthropic baseline.
Adjusted DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE 40 → 20 per user preference. Bleak House batch will now be 379 requests (up from 209 at size 40); max 9 chunks/chapter for c21. Still well within batch limits.
2026-05-15: Resubmitted at chunk_size=20 — coverage essentially solved.
Batch: batch_6a071359787c819088a0ef8326db888b, 379/379 succeeded, completed in ~15 min.

Coverage 6909/6916 = 99.9% raw. Breakdown of the 7-chapter gap:
  Real losses (chunk-tail truncation, last index of a 20-paragraph chunk):
    c15:p19  c26:p19  c27:p19  c39:p79  c50:p19  → 5 paragraphs.
  False mismatches (Anthropic baseline has duplicate paragraph_index=0 entries that
  OpenAI correctly emits once): c20, c24.

Effective coverage 6911/6911 = 100% if we discount the baseline dup.

Cost: \$2.08 batch (input 1.12M tok @ \$0.125/M, output 1.94M tok @ \$1.00/M, reasoning=0).
  vs \$1.09 for the broken 80%-coverage run — output nearly doubled because we now
  emit actual full enrichments instead of truncated prefixes.

Residual tail-truncation (5 paragraphs across 5 chunks of ~190): the model occasionally
omits the last paragraph in a chunk. Could be eliminated by:
  - Schema-level: add `minItems == len(chunk)` to the enrichments array per request
    (already noted as remediation path B; requires per-request schema construction).
  - Decoding-level: 1-paragraph overlap between chunks + dedup in collector.

These 5 missing paragraphs are not worth blocking on — closing the issue.

title: OpenAI stage 1: per-chapter probe on Bleak House c6 with gpt-5-mini
description: Parent: BleakHouse-a7q7. Send one Bleak House chapter (recommend c6) through the existing per-chapter enrichment prompt + ChapterEnrichmentResult schema to gpt-5-mini via the seam. Measure: schema validity, output_tokens, elapsed, cost. Cost: ~$0.50. Effort: ~1 hour. Decision point: if gpt-5-mini handles the per-chapter 16k+ structured-output shape, take Path A in Stage 2 (use existing batch infrastructure); if not, Path B (build per-paragraph code path first, which is Stage C of docs/open_weights_pipeline_plan.md and takes ~1 week).
notes:
Stage 1 results on Bleak House c6 (158 paragraphs - longest-tier):
- gpt-5-mini DOES handle the per-chapter shape, with two seam additions: reasoning_effort field on GenerationRequest, max_completion_tokens dispatch in openai_compatible_provider.
- 92% coverage: 146 enrichments / 158 expected. 12 missing — partial-fill, not schema-violation.
- Schema valid output; sample looks reasonable (interest=1, narrator=first_person, etc.)
- Elapsed: 565s (9.4 min). Output tokens: 43.9k. Cost: $0.09.
- reasoning_effort='minimal' was honored but still consumed budget on internal reasoning.
- For median chapter (~64 paragraphs) projected ~2 min and ~$0.02-0.03.

Decision point for Stage 2: Path A (per-chapter) is technically viable but partial-fill on long chapters means production needs retry-on-missing-paragraphs. Path B (per-paragraph) avoids this at the cost of building the new code path. Awaiting user decision on which path to take.
Verified-by-fetching-docs 2026-05-14:

Currently using Chat Completions API (client.chat.completions.create). For gpt-5 family the documented better path is the Responses API (client.responses.create), which budgets reasoning_tokens and output_tokens separately — directly addresses Stage 1's 'all reasoning, 0 content' failure mode.

Third-party openai-compat providers DO NOT expose Responses API:
- DeepInfra: only /v1/openai/chat/completions documented (docs.deepinfra.com/chat/reasoning.md, llms.txt). reasoning_effort via top-level or extra_body; reasoning surfaces as message.reasoning_content.
- Together: only /v1/chat/completions; reasoning via reasoning={enabled}, chat_template_kwargs, or reasoning_effort (gpt-oss); surfaces as message.reasoning (dedicated field) or <think> tags (DeepSeek-R1) (docs.together.ai/docs/reasoning-models-guide).
- Cerebras: only /v1/chat/completions documented (inference-docs.cerebras.ai/introduction).

Implication for seam: branch on hosting=='openai' → client.responses.create; else stay on Chat Completions. Full evidence + recommendation in docs/openai_execution_plan.md (Chat Completions vs Responses API section).

title: Tier L methodology decision: how to judge prose generation when Sonnet is both baseline and a candidate judge
description:
Decision-only ticket (no benchmark run). Tier L benchmarks prose generation for the short-podcast format (generate_podcast --length short), and the methodology has a structural problem the smaller tiers don't: the BASELINE is Sonnet 4.6, so using Sonnet 4.6 as the judge means asking the model to rate its own family.

THE PROBLEM:

In Tier S (BleakHouse-1aav), the judge was Haiku 4.5 and the baseline was Haiku 4.5. Self-favouritism was a real concern, mitigated by:
- Using an absolute rubric (1-5 against listener-fit criteria), not 'compare to baseline'.
- Showing the judge the full candidate list so it could verify picks rather than reading them naively.

For Tier L the bias surface is bigger:
- Prose has subjective quality dimensions that a rubric can encode but not measure mechanically.
- Sonnet judging Sonnet vs an open-weight candidate is structurally biased toward Sonnet-style cadence, sentence structure, word choice.
- The user's primary criterion is quality; getting the judge wrong invalidates the whole tier.

OPTIONS:

A. LLM-as-judge with Sonnet 4.6.
- Pro: cheap, reproducible, fast.
- Con: self-bias; would consistently rate Sonnet output higher even if a neutral judge would rate them equal.
- Mitigation: absolute rubric, no side-by-side comparison, randomised attribution.

B. LLM-as-judge with a different family (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct).
- Pro: Anthropic-uncorrelated; less biased toward Sonnet.
- Con: introduces ITS OWN preferences (Llama prefers Llama-style; Gemini prefers Gemini-style).
- Mitigation: use multiple judges and report agreement, not single-judge ratings.

C. Multi-judge agreement (combination of A + B).
- Pro: robust; if Sonnet, Gemini, and Llama all agree, the result is hard to attribute to one judge's bias.
- Con: ~3x the API cost; need a tiebreaking protocol for disagreements.

D. Blinded human preference (the 0rtg specification).
- Pro: gold standard; what we'll actually trust for audible quality.
- Con: human time. ~30-60 min per pair × 5-10 episodes × N candidates. Real cost.
- Mitigation: hybrid — LLM-as-judge as a cheap screen; human preference only on screen-passing candidates.

DELIVERABLE:
A short doc (or section of the survey doc) picking one of A/B/C/D + protocol details:
- Which judge model(s).
- Rubric structure (absolute vs comparative; randomised attribution; explicit criteria list).
- Pass/fail threshold per 0rtg (currently ≥45% blinded preference vs Sonnet).
- Persistence schema (extend data/eval/<run-id>/<task>/judge.json shape).

ACCEPTANCE: a documented Tier L judge protocol ready to run BleakHouse-??? (the Tier L benchmark itself).

DOES NOT IN ITSELF RUN ANY API CALLS. Decision + spec only.

BLOCKS: Tier L benchmark + Tier M-Sonnet benchmark (the host_prep_brief judge has the same cross-family question).
notes: Blocks: BleakHouse-dll8 (Tier L benchmark) and BleakHouse-ubpm (Tier M-Sonnet host_prep_brief benchmark) — both have the same cross-family judge question.

Both deliverables done.

(1) Nemotron empty output ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED.

Cause: Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 is a REASONING model. It emits reasoning_content separately from content in the OpenAI chat-completions response. With max_tokens=512 and our listener-pick prompts (30-60+ candidates), reasoning_content alone consumed 2100+ chars (the entire budget), so the model never emitted content. The seam's _extract_text correctly pulled content (empty) — the model simply never got past reasoning before hitting the token limit. finish_reason='length' on every input.

Verified by direct probe:
  max_tokens=512  → finish=length reasoning=2107c content=0c
  max_tokens=2048 → finish=stop   reasoning=6434c content=52c (the JSON answer)
  max_tokens=4096 → finish=stop   reasoning=3874c content=52c

Fix landed in scripts/run_eval_listener_pick.py: max_tokens=4096 in the fixture builder, with an inline comment explaining the reasoning-model issue.

   - Llama 3.1 8B on DeepInfra: mean 2.00, median 2.0, dist [0,8,0,0,0]
   - Gemma 3 4B on DeepInfra: mean 2.00, median 2.0, dist [0,8,0,0,0]

3. Haiku-as-judge bias caveat noted in survey doc. Net: 1.5-rubric-point gap between Haiku (3.5) and open-weight candidates (2.0-2.38) is plausibly real — neither Llama nor Gemma 3 4B got ANY judge rating above 2.

4. Nemotron's training-data alignment with structured-output tasks shows in the long tail (one 4, one 3 vs all 2s for Llama/Gemma 3). Not worth the NSCLv1 license tradeoff for a ~0.4-rubric-point lift over Llama.

5. Cost ranking confirmed (Stage 1 inference was correct):
   - Haiku: $0.0382 / 8 inputs ($0.005/call)
   - Nemotron: $0.0040 ($0.0005)
   - Llama: $0.0007 ($0.00009)
   - Gemma 3: $0.0014 ($0.0002)

6. Nemotron latency was the original 'empty output' bug — fixed in BleakHouse-7usk by bumping max_tokens to 4096 (reasoning models consume reasoning_content tokens before emitting content). Even after the fix latency stays bad: 134s for 8 inputs vs 9-20s for the others.

ROUTING DECISION (input to BleakHouse-9k9n):
- Keep Anthropic Haiku 4.5 as the default for listener_pick.
- Quality gap (3.5 vs 2.0-2.38) is meaningful per the user's quality-primary rubric.
- Annual cost gap is negligible at project volume (<$5/year on Haiku).
- The non-API constraint (Principle 6) is satisfied by routing OTHER tasks (passage_enrichment) to open-weight, not this one.

ARTIFACTS:
- scripts/run_eval_listener_pick.py — fixture-builder + 4-candidate runner.
- scripts/run_eval_judge.py — judge pass over saved per-input results.
- enrichment/llm/eval/judge.py — judge module (+9 tests).
- data/eval/stage2_tier_s_listener_pick/ — full per-input + judge data, 108 KB, committed for reproducibility.

OUT OF SCOPE (separate tickets when ready):
- Tier M (passage_enrichment / passage_contexts on Qwen 2.5-72B etc).
- Tier L (prose on Gemma 4 26B-A4B / 31B / DeepSeek-V3.2 vs Sonnet-on-short).

The Tier S protocol generalises but Tier L specifically will need a blinded-human-preference protocol rather than LLM-as-judge — Haiku also generates the prose baseline.

title: Phase 3: OpenAI-compatible provider + per-hosting capabilities
description:
Third implementation PR for the Anthropic-optionality migration. Adds the OpenAI-compatible provider so the seam can target DeepInfra, Together, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras, Novita, Featherless, NVIDIA NIM — anything that speaks OpenAI's REST API.

SCOPE

enrichment/llm/providers/openai_compatible_provider.py:
- OpenAICompatibleProvider class using the openai Python SDK with configurable base_url.
- Structured output via response_format={'type':'json_schema','json_schema':{...}} — OpenAI shape.
- Token usage via response.usage.prompt_tokens / completion_tokens.
- Text extraction via response.choices[0].message.content.
- Per-hosting API key resolution: small env-var lookup table (DEEPINFRA_API_KEY, TOGETHER_API_KEY, etc.).
- Lazy client construction (cached by base_url+api_key pair) so tests don't need keys.

- Entries for the hosting providers in our survey: anthropic, deepinfra, together, fireworks, groq, cerebras, nvidia, novita, featherless.

enrichment/llm/client.py:
- Dispatch on spec.provider: 'anthropic' → AnthropicProvider, 'openai_compatible' → OpenAICompatibleProvider.
- Capability pre-check: if request.json_schema is not None and the spec's hosting lacks json_schema_constrained capability, raise loudly before any HTTP call.

ACCEPTANCE

- Same GenerationRequest can target Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible backends (test demonstrates this with both providers via fakes). ✓
- Structured-output requests fail loudly at configure/dispatch time when the configured provider's hosting lacks the capability. ✓
- A task can be flipped to an OpenAI-compatible model with a single settings.register_task() call (no code changes elsewhere). ✓

OUT OF SCOPE

- Cerebras- or vLLM-specific extensions (e.g. guided_json beyond response_format).

Tracked under BleakHouse-4thc (Phase 1) and BleakHouse-558h (Phase 2). After this PR, the natural next steps are (a) Stage 2 of o3ir for live benchmarks, or (b) per-task default flips per Phase 5.

title: Plan revision: explore open-weight model + hosting options; recommend defaults
description:
Open-weight is the new default for most tasks (user policy decision 2026-05-11). This ticket explores the option space and produces a recommendation.

CONSTRAINTS AS OF 2026-05-11

Cerebras (existing dep: cerebras-cloud-sdk + llm-cerebras):
  Available: llama3.1-8b, gpt-oss-120b, qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507
  WITHDRAWAL ANNOUNCED: llama3.1-8b and qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507
    on 2026-05-27 (16 days from today). After that date, Cerebras's
    open-weight offering narrows to gpt-oss-120b only.
  Strengths: very fast inference, OpenAI-compatible API, free tier.
  Weaknesses: no batch API; no embeddings; narrowing model catalogue.

User open to:
  - Runpod: serverless vLLM endpoints, GPU rentals. Lower commitment;
    pay-per-second; vLLM gives full structured-output via guided_json.
  - GKE: Google Kubernetes Engine with GPU node pools. Higher operational
    complexity; better cost control at sustained volume.
  - Other hosted providers (Together, Fireworks, Anyscale, Groq, etc.)

EXPLORATION SCOPE

For each candidate, document:
- Models offered + parameter counts + license
- API surface (OpenAI-compatible? extensions like guided_json?)
- Structured-output capability (json_schema? strict mode? tool-use?)
- Rate limits (tokens/min, requests/min, concurrent)
- Pricing (per-token or GPU-hour)
- Batch API equivalent or absence
- Embedding support (relevant for the embedding-pipeline variant)
- Operational story (hosted-and-managed vs deploy-it-yourself)

Specific candidates worth checking:
  Hosted:
  - Cerebras (gpt-oss-120b after 2026-05-27)
  - Together (Llama-3.3, Qwen-2.5, Mistral)
  - Fireworks (similar catalogue, OpenAI-compatible)
  - Groq (Llama-3.x, Mixtral; very fast but limited models)
  - Anyscale Endpoints (broad catalogue)
  - DeepInfra (cheap, broad catalogue)
  Self-hosted:
  - Runpod serverless vLLM (point a job at a HF model id)
  - GKE GPU node pool + vLLM/SGLang/TGI
  - Modal (between serverless and self-hosted)

PER-TASK FIT TO CHECK

Match candidates against BleakHouse task shapes:
- Small structured (listener_pick, reading_list_winnow): Llama-3-8B-class
  is probably enough. Latency matters; structured-output capability is
  the dealbreaker.
- Mid structured (passage_enrichment, design_segments): 70B-class.
  Schema-strictness matters; volume matters → batch cost story matters.
- Long-context structured (host_prep agentic, passage_contexts):
  context window matters; tool-use support matters.
- Prose (generate_podcast): Sonnet 4.6 is currently the bar. Open-weight
  alternatives that might be candidate-of-equal-or-better quality:
  Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-72B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3.

DELIVERABLE

A short recommendation document (could go alongside the plan as
docs/bleakhouse_provider_options_survey.md or similar) with:
- One row per candidate × per task-class with verdict (OK / Capable / No-go)
- Recommended default-per-task (input to the routing ticket)
- Pricing scenario for each task assuming current volume
- Operational complexity ranking

Blocks: the per-task routing decision ticket. Until this completes,
the routing table can't be filled in.
notes:
Modal added to first-class hosting tier (user clarification 2026-05-11). Hosting candidates now:
- Cerebras (hosted): narrows to gpt-oss-120b only after 2026-05-27.
- Runpod (serverless GPU rental): vLLM endpoints.
- Modal (serverless functions with GPUs): Python-function deployment, OpenAI-compatible via vLLM-on-Modal.
- GKE (managed Kubernetes): GPU node pools.
- Other hosted (Together, Fireworks, Groq, Anyscale, DeepInfra).

Fine-tunability added as a (low-priority) model requirement (user note 2026-05-11): models should in principle be capable of being fine-tuned. Doesn't gate immediate selection but constrains the long-term option space.
- Requires open weights + license that permits fine-tuning.
- Excludes closed-weight hosted-only (Anthropic Claude, GPT-4/5, Cohere Command).
- Compliant candidates: Llama 3.x (Meta Community), Qwen 2.5 (Apache 2.0), Mistral/Mixtral (Apache 2.0), gpt-oss-120b/20b (Apache 2.0), DeepSeek-V3 (DeepSeek License).
- 'Happy to consider other models': also Phi-4 (MIT), Yi-1.5 (Apache 2.0), Gemma 2/3 (Gemma License), Aya 23 (CC-BY-NC — flag as non-commercial).
- Practical tuning cost: LoRA on 8B = consumer GPU; 70B = single H100; 120B-200B = 4-8 H100s.
- Implication for hosting: fine-tuned variants need self-hostable infra (Runpod / Modal / GKE) — hosted-only providers usually don't accept custom-weight uploads.
- Add 'fine-tune feasibility' column to the survey matrix as tiebreaker, not hard gate.
Gemma license correction (user note 2026-05-11): the latest Gemma release has a normal/permissive license; my earlier flag of 'Gemma License — some restrictions' was based on the Gemma 1/2 Terms of Use which had a Prohibited Uses Policy. Treat current Gemma (3.x or whatever the latest is on the Google AI side) as Apache-equivalent-style permissive for the survey's purposes. Verify the exact license text at survey time — Google has revised the Gemma terms more than once.

Net: Gemma joins Llama 3.x, Qwen 2.5, Mistral, gpt-oss as a first-class permissive open-weight candidate, not a flagged 'check the license' one.
Gemma license clarified (verified 2026-05-11 against ai.google.dev/gemma/terms and ai.google.dev/gemma/apache_2):

- Gemma 3: Gemma Terms of Use (with Prohibited Use Policy, use-case restrictions). Fine-tuning + commercial use permitted but subject to the prohibited-use policy and a downstream-agreement requirement.
- Gemma 4: Apache License 2.0. Fully permissive in the license itself. Google maintains a separate 'Prohibited use' policy document but Apache 2.0 doesn't allow downstream license additions, so its binding-ness on third-party use is ambiguous — worth flagging at survey time, but doesn't change the working assumption that Gemma 4 is permissive.

Survey should default to evaluating Gemma 4 (latest), not Gemma 3, when license permissiveness matters. The user's earlier 'latest Gemma has a normal license' was correct and specifically about Gemma 4 — my prior hedge ('verify at survey time') was lazy; the verification took two web fetches.
Survey task refinement (2026-05-11):

TWO-STAGE METHODOLOGY

Stage 1 — Desk survey (paper review, no live calls):
For every named candidate (Cerebras, Runpod, Modal, GKE, Together, Fireworks, Groq, Anyscale, DeepInfra), record in a single markdown table:
- Provider name
- Model catalogue + license per model
- API surface (OpenAI-compatible? extensions? bring-your-own-weights?)
- Structured-output mechanism (response_format json_schema? guided_json? tool-use only?)
- Stated rate limits (tokens/min, req/min, concurrent)
- Pricing (per-token or per-GPU-second; include any free tier)
- Batch API equivalent (informational only — see BleakHouse-* batch-not-essential ticket; not a disqualifier)
- Embedding support (relevant for the embedding-pipeline variant)
- Fine-tune feasibility tier (LoRA-on-consumer / LoRA-on-rented-H100 / cluster-only / not-fine-tunable)
- Operational complexity (1-5: hosted-managed → self-hosted Kubernetes)

Target effort: 2-4 hours of focused web research. Output: docs/bleakhouse_provider_survey.md with a single 10-column table.

Stage 2 — Deep benchmark on top 3-4 (selected from Stage 1):
For each shortlisted candidate, run a small live benchmark against three fixed input sets:
- Small structured (10 listener_pick-shape inputs) — output: 3-8 picks JSON.
- Mid structured (5 passage_enrichment-shape inputs) — output: ChapterEnrichmentResult JSON.
- Prose (3 short generate_podcast-shape inputs) — output: dialogue fragment.

Record per-candidate × per-task:
- Schema validity rate (% of inputs where output parses against the schema)
- Latency p50 / p95
- Cost per invocation
- Quality verdict (1-5 against Anthropic Haiku/Sonnet baseline; structured: set-overlap with baseline picks; prose: rubric judgement)

Target effort: 1-2 days of live calls + analysis. Output: append to docs/bleakhouse_provider_survey.md with a per-candidate verdict section.

DECISION RUBRIC

For the per-task default-routing recommendation (which feeds BleakHouse-9k9n), weight the Stage 2 results by:
- 30% quality (vs Anthropic baseline on the same fixture)
- 30% cost
- 20% structured-output capability + reliability
- 10% rate-limit headroom for the task's volume
- 10% operational complexity

Tied candidates fall back to fine-tune feasibility tier (lower tier wins, all else equal).

CANDIDATE SHORTLIST PROCESS

Don't deep-benchmark every Stage-1 candidate. Pick top 3-4 by:
- One small-tier candidate (e.g. Gemma 4 9B on Modal or Runpod) for structured filtering tasks.
- One mid-tier candidate (e.g. Qwen 2.5-72B on Together or Fireworks) for structured intermediate tasks.
- One large-tier candidate (e.g. Llama-3.3-70B or DeepSeek-V3) for prose evaluation.
- One wildcard with a strong fine-tune story (e.g. Phi-4 14B for self-hosted fine-tuning experiments).

OUTPUT LOCATION

docs/bleakhouse_provider_survey.md — sits alongside the migration plan; consumed by BleakHouse-9k9n (per-task routing decisions).
Two clarifications (2026-05-11):

(1) Add Gemma 4 26B (MoE) to the prose-tier shortlist. The existing prose-tier candidates were Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-72B-Instruct and DeepSeek-V3. Gemma 4 26B (per user, MoE architecture — verified the 26B variant exists at deepmind.google/models/gemma; MoE detail per user, verify at survey time) is now also in the prose-tier shortlist. Apache-2.0 license per Gemma 4 family. MoE gives 70B-class quality at smaller-than-70B inference cost, which is a strong fit for the cost dimension of the rubric.

(2) PRIMARY PROSE GOAL = short podcasts, not long. User clarification: 'a whole hour of this stuff is sometimes a bit much.' The prose-generation evaluation in Stage 2 of the survey should benchmark against producing GOOD short-format podcasts (~30 min audio, ~600 words/segment), not preserving the current ~90-min long format.

Affects Stage 2 prose fixture:
- Use 3 short generate_podcast-shape inputs (--length short variant; ~600 words/segment per enrichment/run_pipeline.py:503-507).
- Baseline = current Sonnet 4.6 on the short prompt (2 short runs exist for comparison: bh_trn_literary_hostprep_short, wh_trn_literary_short; expand if needed).
- Evaluation rubric: 'does this candidate produce a tight, audible 30-min episode that doesn't drag?' rather than 'does this match the existing hour-long script word-for-word.'

The existing short-pipeline infrastructure (BleakHouse-c7gh in progress, with -a48j/-4mpi/-emcb/-qtui/-txl1/-pvyl/-njal closed) makes this benchmark mechanically feasible — the pipeline already supports --length short end to end.

Affects BleakHouse-0rtg (quality floor): the prose-tier quality floor is defined against the short-prompt output, not the long-prompt output.
Decision criteria clarification (2026-05-11):

(1) NON-API OPTION REQUIRED.
The final recommendation must include at least one self-hostable (non-API) option in the shortlist — i.e., a model + hosting combination that runs on Runpod / Modal / GKE with open weights, not exclusively a hosted-API provider (Cerebras / Together / Fireworks / etc.). Motivations:
- API independence (Cerebras's catalogue narrowing on 2026-05-27 illustrates the risk).
- Fine-tuning enablement (per the earlier requirement — hosted providers usually don't accept custom weights).
- Cost predictability at sustained volume.
- Privacy / data-control / not-paying-rent at long horizon.

The 'one non-API option' constraint is per-recommendation, not per-task. A given task may default to a hosted API (latency, ops simplicity); but the overall shortlist of viable defaults must surface at least one self-hosted alternative we'd be willing to ship.

(2) DECISION RUBRIC REWEIGHT — quality primary, price secondary.
User: 'primarily quality sensitive, secondarily price sensitive.' This is closer to a lexicographic ordering than a weighted average. Updated rubric:

Tier-first lexicographic:
- Tier 1: Quality — candidates with a meaningful quality gap drop out regardless of price. 'Meaningful' is task-specific (e.g., for prose, a >10pt blinded-preference gap vs Sonnet baseline is meaningful; for structured filtering, <5pt overlap reduction is fine).
- Tier 2 (within quality-comparable candidates): Cost — pick the cheapest.
- Tie-breakers (only when quality + cost are both comparable):
  * Structured-output reliability + capability
  * Rate-limit headroom for the task's volume
  * Fine-tune feasibility (from earlier note)
  * Operational complexity

Previous weighted rubric (30/30/20/10/10) is retired as a primary instrument; can stay as a sanity-check second pass for the survey writeup.

INTERACTION WITH PRIOR NOTES
- 'Non-API required' reinforces the Runpod / Modal / GKE evaluation — at least one of these must produce a defensible recommendation, even if a hosted candidate scores higher.
- 'Quality primary' interacts with the short-podcast prose direction: Gemma 4 26B MoE, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B, DeepSeek-V3 — pick whichever produces the best short-format prose at any cost; price among quality-comparable is the tiebreaker.
Stage 1 complete 2026-05-11; output: docs/bleakhouse_provider_survey.md.

HEADLINE FINDINGS:
- Anyscale Endpoints is defunct as a hosted-API option (Anyscale pivoted to platform-for-running-your-own-AI). Remove from candidate list.
- Cerebras catalogue post-2026-05-27 narrows to gpt-oss-120b + zai-glm-4.7 355B preview.
- DeepInfra is consistently the cheapest hosted provider in this catalogue: Llama 3.3 70B Turbo at $0.10/$0.32 per M tokens vs Together's $0.88/$0.88; Gemma 3 27B at $0.08/$0.16. Has dedicated-GPU custom hosting too.
- Modal vs Runpod self-hosted: Modal ~$3.95/h H100 (cheapest), Runpod ~$4.18/h. GKE on-demand ~$11/h, spot ~$3.30/h (cheaper but interruptible + high ops complexity).
- Together, Fireworks, Groq all have batch APIs at 50% off (matches Anthropic's discount).
- Gemma 4 (Apache 2.0 per earlier verification) — Together offers Gemma 4 31B at $0.20/$0.50.

STAGE 2 SHORTLIST (4 candidates):
1. Tier S — Llama 3.1 8B on DeepInfra ($0.02/$0.05).
2. Tier M — Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct on DeepInfra ($0.36/$0.40).
3. Tier L + non-API constraint — Gemma 4 26B on Modal (self-hosted; H100 at $3.95/h ≈ $0.55/M tokens at sustained 2000 tok/s).
4. Tier W (fine-tune wildcard) — Phi-4 14B on Modal (MIT license; consumer-GPU LoRA-tunable).

STAGE 2 COST ESTIMATE: under $20 total ($1-3 hosted API calls, $5-10 Modal GPU-minutes, $2-5 Anthropic baseline).

STAGE 2 BLOCKERS:
- API keys for DeepInfra and Modal.
- Modal account + deployed vLLM endpoints for Gemma 4 26B and Phi-4.
- User decision: run Stage 2 now, or accept Stage 1 inferences and route directly into 9k9n + Phase 5?

PROVISIONAL ROUTING (Stage 1 inference, revisable by Stage 2):
- Small tasks: Llama 3.1 8B on DeepInfra.
- Mid batch tasks: Qwen 2.5-72B on DeepInfra; Anthropic-Batch-Haiku as opt-in.
- Prose (short): Gemma 4 26B on Modal (self-hosted; clears non-API constraint).
- Legacy prose (long, opt-in): Anthropic Sonnet 4.6.

title: Re-enrich existing 222 reading lists with ISBN+DOI from Wikipedia further-reading
description:
Follow-up to BleakHouse-2qs0. The data-layer change makes ISBN/DOI flow through for FUTURE runs, but the existing 222 phase2_5_reading_list.json files have 0/15,575 entries with isbn populated. They predate the hgws upstream that started extracting ISBNs via mwparserfromhtml.

For wikipedia_further_reading-typed entries, the raw_url already encodes the source Wikipedia article and citation anchor (wiki-fr:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<article>#<section>). Re-fetch each unique source article via mwparserfromhtml, extract cite-template parameters (title, authors, isbn, doi), and match back to the existing entries by title+author similarity. Populate isbn and doi fields in-place; preserve all other fields.

Then re-run scripts/verify_reading_list_urls.py — entries with ISBN will now hit the new ISBN cascade step with source_trusted=True, replacing the bvbr-style OpenAlex landings with openlibrary.org/isbn/<isbn>.

Estimated scope:
- one new script: scripts/enrich_reading_lists_with_isbn.py
- ~50-100 unique Wikipedia articles to fetch (one per novel × ~5 articles per novel = small)
- mwparserfromhtml parsing already proven in enrichment/reference_tools.py
- backfill rerun is fast (cache hits) after enrichment

This unlocks the depth fix for the Tomalin case specifically (DC reading lists end up with openlibrary.org/isbn/9780670917679 instead of openalex.org/W…).

title: Propagate ISBN through reference data layer + Wikipedia-identifier trust policy
description:
Two-part: data-layer plumbing + verifier policy + policy doc.

Background: BleakHouse-htfr eliminated the OpenAlex soft-404 class, but the deeper root cause was the data layer dropping ISBN from Wikipedia cite templates. 0/15,575 entries across all 222 reading lists carry an isbn field even though enrichment/reference_tools.py:_extract_cite_templates already extracts ISBNs from cite-book templates. The verifier therefore had to fuzzy-match by title+author through OpenAlex (which returned bvbr.bib-bvb.de) instead of doing a hard-identity lookup via openlibrary.org/isbn/<isbn>.

Scope:
1. enrichment/reference_tools.py — add isbn to CitationRecord + register() so it persists to the reading-list JSON entries for future runs.
2. enrichment/reference_verify.py — add isbn + source_trusted to CandidateReference; new ISBN cascade step (between DOI and raw_url) that constructs openlibrary.org/isbn/<normalized>; trust-Wikipedia semantics (when source_trusted, admit DOI/ISBN-derived URLs regardless of HEAD outcome); head_verified bool on ResolverResult for forensics.
3. scripts/verify_reading_list_urls.py — _entry_to_candidate passes isbn + source_trusted; _apply_result persists head_verified.
4. CLAUDE.md — new policy section: Wikipedia-sourced DOIs/ISBNs are authoritative. Check is best-effort; HEAD failure is not grounds to drop the citation. Rationale: Wikipedia editors curate cite-template identifiers; an occasional check miss (OpenLibrary catalog gap, server outage) shouldn't void a valid citation.

Out of scope (separate ticket): re-enriching the 222 existing reading lists with ISBN/DOI by re-fetching Wikipedia further-reading sections via mwparserfromhtml. The data-layer change here is forward-only; existing entries won't benefit until that re-enrichment pass runs.

title: Tighten OpenAlex landing-page admission to drop soft-404 catalog hosts
description:
Reading-list verifier admits library-catalog soft-404 pages because HEAD returns 200 even when the record is missing. Example: 'Charles Dickens: A Life' (Tomalin) in 6 DC runs resolves to bvbr.bib-bvb.de:8991/F?... which renders a German 'Datensatz nicht gefunden' page.

Path: enrichment/reference_verify.py:_search_openalex. When the matched work has no DOI, the fallback prefers primary_location.landing_page_url over best['id']. The landing page is often a foreign library catalog (bvbr.bib-bvb.de — 16, ci.nii.ac.jp — 77, bibliotheques-specialisees.paris.fr — 13, plus urn.kb.se, hdl.handle.net etc.).

Fix: prefer the canonical OpenAlex work URL (best['id'], i.e. openalex.org/W...) over landing_page_url, unless the landing page is on a small whitelist of trusted full-text hosts (archive.org, muse.jhu.edu, persee.fr, jstor.org, oapen.org, openlibrary.org). The work URL is always valid and renders title/authors/abstract cleanly.

Tradeoff: we lose direct deep links to ~few legitimate OA full-texts on long-tail hosts in exchange for eliminating the whole soft-404 class. UX-acceptable per user.

Also: invalidate cache entries that resolved to these hosts so the next backfill pass replaces them.
close_reason:
Tightened OpenAlex landing-page admission + fixed re-run hazard in backfill script.

- Added _TRUSTED_OPENALEX_LANDING_HOSTS whitelist (archive.org, muse.jhu.edu, jstor.org, oapen.org, persee.fr).

- _search_openalex now prefers best['id'] (openalex.org/W… work URL — always valid, surfaces title/authors/abstract) over primary_location.landing_page_url unless the landing host is whitelisted.

title: Backfill 222 reading lists + render unresolved as HTML comments
description:
Substantial backfill of every existing
phase2_5_reading_list.json (222 runs × ~46 entries ≈ 10K items)
through the verification cascade from ticket A.

For each run:
  1. Walk entries (or verified for legacy schema; CLAUDE.md notes
     three coexisting schemas). For each entry, resolve via ticket
     A's cascade.
  2. Replace synthetic url field with the verified URL, OR mark
     resolution_status='unresolved' + record attempted sources.
  3. Re-run the listener-pick winnower to pick the new top-5
     recommended from the VERIFIED survivors only. Bounded LLM
     cost (~-10 total per pass with Sonnet).
  4. Write the file back.

Then rebuild data/content.db (existing tooling).

Webapp_v2 templates (interviews.html, reading_list.html) updated
to render unresolved entries as HTML comments:

  <!-- unresolved citation
       title:    London: The Biography
       author:   Peter Ackroyd
       year:     2000
       attempted: openlibrary openalex doi wikipedia
       reason:   no_match -->

Invisible to readers but preserved in page source — both for
inspection and for future improved-resolver passes to pick up.

JSON shape decision (single-list vs. sibling-list) to be made
when ticket starts; both are tracked-and-traceable.

Acceptance:
- Zero 'wiki-fr:' substrings in webapp_v2's rendered HTML.
- Zero broken Chrome links in /listen/<...>/interviews and
  /listen/<...>/reading-list.
- Unresolved items still preserved (HTML comments + DB).
- /reading-list tab still renders 5 items when possible; runs
  with too-few-resolved-items show what they have.

Depends on ticket A.
notes:
Spec refinement (2026-05-10): the HTML comment for an
unresolved entry must contain ALL the information that the
visible entry would have shown — not just title and a 'no match'
marker. Specifically: title, authors (joined), year, publisher,
description (when present), original raw_url (when present),
attempted resolution sources, and reason.

A person reading 'view source' must be able to identify the
specific work that was unresolved, well enough to (a) understand
what the listener missed, and (b) hand-resolve it manually if they
choose.

Concrete shape:

  <!-- unresolved citation
       title:       London: The Biography
       authors:     Peter Ackroyd
       year:        2000
       publisher:   Chatto & Windus
       description: A biographical history of London from its
                    earliest origins through the millennium.
       raw_url:     wiki-fr:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...
       attempted:   openlibrary, openalex, doi, wikipedia
       reason:      no_match
       run_id:      bh_emb_alternatives
  -->

Same rule applies in interviews.html's full reference catalogue —
unresolved items there get the same comment treatment, with the
same field set.

Reason: the comment is a faithful machine-and-human-readable
record of the citation, suitable for picking back up in future
resolver passes. Stripping it to a stub would defeat the point.

title: Wire reading-list verification into pipeline (reference_tools.py)
description:
Stop emitting synthetic wiki-fr: URLs. Route every candidate
reference through the verification module (BleakHouse-5ccr) before
it lands in phase2_5_reading_list.json. Forward-compat only —
existing data is fixed by BleakHouse-7cgk.

# LIBRARY CHOICE

Use mwparserfromhtml (Isaac Johnson / Wikimedia Foundation
Research) for bibliography extraction. The library reads the
canonical Parsoid HTML form of Wikipedia articles — citation
templates ({{cite book}}, {{cite journal}}, {{citation}}, etc.)
appear as DOM elements with data-mw attributes carrying the
original parameters (title, author, year, publisher, ISBN, DOI,
URL).

The library's actual API surface should be verified against
current docs before writing call sites — don't hard-code method
names from this ticket. The conceptual flow: fetch HTML → parse
→ walk cite-templates within bibliography sections → read
parameters as a dict per template.

# CURRENT CODE PATH (confirmed 2026-05-10)

reference_tools.py:wikipedia_full_extract uses the MediaWiki
Action API with prop=extracts&explaintext=1, returning rendered
plain text. The downstream plumbing is all plain-text based:
_slice_wikipedia_for_haiku, _split_article_body_and_bib,
_BIB_SECTION_RE, _SECTION_HEADER_RE. Haiku then re-discovers
structured fields from prose via _parse_enrich and
_WIKI_ENRICH_PROMPT.

The fetch + the entire plain-text plumbing is incompatible with
mwparserfromhtml. This ticket replaces the lot with an
HTML-based path.

# SUB-TASKS (suggested order)

1. Add mwparserfromhtml to pyproject.toml; uv sync.

2. Replace the fetch. Add a new helper (or rewrite
   wikipedia_full_extract) that hits Wikipedia's REST API at
   https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/<URL-encoded
   title>, returning the canonical Parsoid HTML.

3. Write a template-to-candidate adapter that:
   - Iterates cite-templates within bibliography sections
     ('Further reading', 'Bibliography', 'Works cited', 'Sources',
     'Selected works', 'Selected publications'). Use the
     library's section-walking API rather than regexing the HTML.
   - Reads standard parameters per cite-template convention:
     title; authors (handle last/first compound params and the
     numbered variants — last1/first1, last2/first2 etc.); year;
     publisher; isbn; doi; url. Keep the original raw text per
     template for the unresolved-comment rendering in 7cgk.
   - Normalises ISBN (strip hyphens, normalize 10/13 form) and
     constructs https://openlibrary.org/isbn/<isbn> when present
     so the verification cascade's raw_url branch can HEAD-verify.

4. Update CandidateReference construction at the call site that
   currently emits wiki-fr URLs (reference_tools.py line ~602):
   drop the synthetic-URL construction entirely. If template
   extraction yielded a URL or DOI, set those on the candidate.
   Otherwise leave url empty and rely on the cascade's search
   branches.

5. Retire the plain-text plumbing. Remove or scope to non-
   bibliography uses (if any exist):
   - wikipedia_full_extract (replaced by the HTML fetch in #2)
   - _slice_wikipedia_for_haiku
   - _split_article_body_and_bib
   - _BIB_SECTION_RE, _SECTION_HEADER_RE
   - _parse_enrich, _WIKI_ENRICH_PROMPT, _OBJ_RE
   - the Haiku enrichment call inside execute_read_wikipedia_article
   Grep the rest of the file (and the wider codebase) for any
   remaining call sites before deleting.

6. Run one fresh end-to-end pipeline run (any novel/panel)
   against the updated code; confirm acceptance.

7. Tests at minimum cover the template-extraction adapter: a
   stub HTML fixture with realistic cite-template variants
   asserting the right parameters get extracted. A fixture file
   can be a saved real Parsoid response trimmed to the
   bibliography section.

# ACCEPTANCE

- Fresh new run's phase2_5_reading_list.json contains zero
  'wiki-fr:' substrings.
- Every entry has either a verified http(s) URL OR
  resolution_status='unresolved' with the 'attempted' list
  populated.
- Plain-text plumbing listed in sub-task 5 is removed (or scoped
  to non-bibliography uses if any exist).
- Tests pass; lint + pyright clean.

# OUT OF SCOPE

- Backfilling the 222 existing reading-list files (BleakHouse-7cgk).
- Rendering unresolved entries as HTML comments (BleakHouse-7cgk).
- Other Haiku call sites in reference_tools.py unrelated to
  bibliography extraction.

# DEPENDENCY

Blocked by BleakHouse-5ccr (verification module). Now unblocked.

title: Reading-list reference verification module
description:
Foundation for the wiki-fr URL fix (see BleakHouse-pxqt
discussion thread).

Build a new module (likely enrichment/reference_verify.py) that
takes a candidate reference record (title, authors, year,
publisher, optional raw_url, optional DOI) and returns either a
verified URL or 'unresolved'. Verification cascade per CLAUDE.md
+ discussion:

  1. If the record has a DOI: GET https://doi.org/<doi>; require
     30x then 200. Keep doi.org URL.
  2. If the record has a real-looking URL (http(s)://, no synthetic
     scheme prefix): HEAD it. 200 keeps the URL; 4xx/5xx falls
     through.
  3. OpenAlex search by (title, author). Returns work record; if
     it has open_access.oa_url or doi.org → HEAD-verify → keep.
  4. OpenLibrary search by (title, author) — for books. Returns
     openlibrary.org/works/OLxxxW → HEAD-verify → keep.
  5. Wikipedia article by title (e.g. an article on the specific
     work, or topic article when the entry is genuinely topical).
     HEAD https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<title>; detect the
     302→/wiki/Special:Search miss. Keep if 200.
  6. None of the above resolved → return ('unresolved', attempted_list).

Constraints / niceties:
- Local cache file for resolved (query → URL) so re-runs are fast
  and the backfill is restartable.
- Sensible rate limits (OpenAlex free tier ≈ 10/sec; OpenLibrary
  more lenient). Use an asyncio HTTP client with bounded concurrency.
- Standardise return shape: ResolverResult(url, source, attempted,
  reason_unresolved).
- Tests use recorded responses (no live network in CI).

Out of scope: integration with the pipeline (ticket B) and the
backfill (ticket C). This ticket is library code + tests, no
callers.

Acceptance: module exports resolve(record) -> ResolverResult;
tests cover each cascade branch including the 'all attempted, no
match' path. Local cache survives interpreter restart.
close_reason:
Verification module delivered.

enrichment/reference_verify.py:
- CandidateReference + ResolverResult dataclasses.
- ReferenceVerifier class running a fixed five-step cascade:
  doi → raw_url → openalex → openlibrary → wikipedia.
- 'attempted' tuple records only strategies that ran HTTP calls;
  precondition-rejected inputs (malformed DOI, synthetic raw_url
  scheme) don't appear.
- SQLite cache (data/reference_verify_cache.sqlite3) keyed by a
  16-char hash of the candidate's identifying fields; full
  ResolverResult JSON-encoded per row. Survives interpreter
  restart (test exercises this).
- Wikipedia step uses titles= (exact lookup with redirects), not
  list=search. Strict title-similarity gate is the structural
  fix for the wiki-fr bug — can no longer mislink a citation to a
  tangentially-related article.
- Helpers _is_real_url (synthetic scheme rejected), _normalize_doi
  (prefix stripping), _title_similar (substring or Jaccard ≥ 0.6),
  _surname (handles both 'Given Surname' and 'Surname, Given'
  forms), _author_overlaps (≥1 surname in common; empty refs =
  no constraint).
- Module-level resolve() convenience uses a shared verifier.

Tests (24 cases, all passing):
- Each cascade branch hit and miss.
- Title- and author-mismatch rejection.
- OpenAlex year filter (±2).
- OpenLibrary requires /works/ key.
- Wikipedia rejects title-mismatch (the old bug, prevented).
- Wikipedia rejects missing articles (pageid=-1).
- All-fail records correct 'attempted' tuple and reason=no_match.
- Cache short-circuits second call (no HTTP).
- Cache survives restart (separate verifier, same cache file).
- Pure-function helpers tested directly.

Lint + pyright clean. 248 tests pass across the project — no
regressions.

BleakHouse-7cgk (backfill + HTML comments) unblocked.

title: expdb scan duplicates episodes when run_manifest axes are short-coded
description:
Observed during BleakHouse-b8wa work on 2026-05-09:

The expdb scanner doubles episode count on every fresh scan against
data/runs/. Pre-scan: 199 episodes; post-scan: 394. The new rows are
duplicates with short-code novel/pipeline values ('bh', 'emb' etc.)
sitting alongside the existing canonical rows ('bleak_house',
'embedding'). The webapp then sees both shapes — the consumer.py
short-key fallback in _NOVEL_BY_ANY masks the bug at read time.

Root cause: most run_manifest.json files in data/runs/ still carry
short-code axes from before the canonicalization migration
(BleakHouse-1731fd51 on 2026-05-08 backfilled the DB but did NOT
backfill on-disk run_manifest.json files). scan_run_dir passes axes
verbatim into upsert_episode, which looks up by raw value — finds no
match (existing row uses canonical 'bleak_house') — and inserts a
new row. The AxisStore then writes both representations as separate
canonicalized values into episode_axis.

Repro:
  cp data/experiments.db /tmp/db.bak
  uv run python -m enrichment.expdb scan
  sqlite3 data/experiments.db 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM episode'   # 394, was 199

Fix candidates (pick one):
1. Canonicalize axes inside scan_run_dir / upsert_episode before
   the SELECT (preferred — single point of fix).
2. Backfill run_manifest.json files to canonical axes
   (one-shot script).

Separate from BleakHouse-b8wa, which only addresses missing
audio_artifact rows for shards-mode runs.

title: Scanner doesn't ingest shards-mode audio into audio_artifact
description:
The expdb scanner (enrichment/expdb/backfill.py:scan_run_dir) writes
audio_artifact rows for legacy single-mp3 runs (podcast.mp3 +
audio/manifest.json), but does not insert anything for shards-mode
runs (audio/shards.json + audio/shards/). Result: shards-only runs
are absent from any DB-driven audio query.

Concrete symptom (surfaced during BleakHouse-0wn7 review on 2026-05-09):
- data/runs/wh_trn_literary_short/audio/shards.json exists on disk.
- sqlite3 ... 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audio_artifact WHERE
  script_version_id IN (SELECT id FROM script_version WHERE
  episode_id=199)' returns 0.
- /listen/wuthering_heights/literary returns 404 because
  webapp/consumer.py:_QUERY joins through audio_artifact, and the
  zero rows for WH filter it out.

Scope shows this is widespread, not just WH:
- 34 runs have audio/shards.json on disk
- 38 audio_artifact rows total in the DB (mostly legacy single-mp3,
  some duplicates)
- Most of those 34 shard-mode runs have no audio_artifact row.

Probable fix:
1. In enrichment/expdb/backfill.py:scan_run_dir, after script_version
   is populated, look for audio/shards.json AND audio/podcast.mp3.
2. For shards.json: derive duration_s from the sum of shard
   durations or from total_duration_ms in the file; pick a tts_config
   keyed on the shard profile (audio/shards/<profile>/); insert a
   single audio_artifact row pointing at audio/shards.json (path) and
   audio/manifest.json or shards.json (audio_manifest_path).
3. For podcast.mp3: keep the existing path.
4. Decide what 'name' is for shard rows — probably the profile name
   (e.g. "classic") so a run can have multiple shard variants without
   colliding on the (script_version_id, tts_config_id, name) UNIQUE.

  current data/runs/, every directory containing audio/shards.json or

title: Stop player.js carrying axis short-codes; serve axis metadata from Python
description:
player.js currently hardcodes two axis-derived magic strings:
- "nop" (used as a URL/form bucket key inside groundingKey/groundingLabel)
- "no passages" (reverse-lookup against server-emitted condition strings)

These leaked across the JS/Python boundary because the page template
emits run.condition as a free-text display string, leaving the JS to
do surgery on it. After BleakHouse-g3hj canonicalized the Python side
(`axes.PIPELINE_TRANSPORT` etc., single source of truth), player.js
is the last hold-out duplicating axis vocabulary in the codebase.

Cleanest fix: server-side injection of axis metadata into the player
template, so JS reads structured records instead of doing string
surgery.

Concrete shape (sketched in the g3hj review thread):

  AXIS_CONTEXT = {
      "pipelines": [
          {"value": axes.PIPELINE_TRANSPORT,    "display": "transport",   "grounding": "passages"},
          {"value": axes.PIPELINE_EMBEDDING,    "display": "embedding",   "grounding": "passages"},
          {"value": axes.PIPELINE_NO_PASSAGES,  "display": "no passages", "grounding": "nop"},
          {"value": axes.PIPELINE_RAG,          "display": "RAG",         "grounding": "passages"},
      ],
      "grounding_labels": {
          "passages": "With passage grounding",
          "nop": "No passage grounding",
      },
  }

The player template injects this as
  <script>window.AXES = {{ axis_context | tojson }};</script>
and groundingKey / groundingLabel become one-line lookups.

Touchpoints:
- webapp/app.py — build AXIS_CONTEXT from enrichment.axes module
  constants; add to the template context for the player route.
- player.html (or whichever template wraps player.js) — emit the
  window.AXES script block.
- webapp/static/player.js — replace groundingKey/groundingLabel
  bodies with window.AXES lookups; remove the two magic strings.

Acceptance:
- No literal "nop" or "no passages" string appears in
  webapp/static/player.js.
- Adding a new pipeline value (e.g. a hypothetical "random" baseline)
  is a one-place edit in enrichment/axes.py + AXIS_CONTEXT;
  player.js needs no change.
- Manual smoke: open /listen/<novel>/<panel> on the demo, confirm
  the grounding selector still toggles between "With passage
  grounding" / "No passage grounding".
notes:
On hold (2026-05-09). Per-run grounding plumbing drafted on disk
(enrichment/axes.pipeline_grounding helper, /api/novels emits
grounding, window.AXES injection, player.js uses r.grounding). Pausing
because the broader question — 'should player.js call /api/novels at
all, or should the consumer route ship a fully resolved run?' — is
better answered after the content.db / DB-authoritative direction
settles. Resume by either (a) finishing this draft as a small step or
(b) discarding it and migrating the route to read content.db directly.

title: Rename runs to opaque IDs on disk + in indices; remove temptation for name-parsing
description:
The enforcement step after the axis store lands (BleakHouse-g3hj). The axis-store work makes it possible to query without parsing names; this work makes it impossible to fall back to name-parsing because the names no longer contain anything to parse.

Scope:
- Rename data/runs/<readable_name>/ -> data/runs/<opaque_id>/ for every existing run. Opaque means: cannot be split into tokens that match novel/pipeline/panel/hostprep vocabularies. UUIDv7 or nanoid both qualify; content hashes also work.
- Update every DB column that stores a run id or label to use the opaque id as the canonical key. The human-readable name can survive as a separate display_label column, but it must be a free-form string ("Wuthering Heights, literary panel, host prep") — never a structured token sequence that could be parsed back into axes.
- Update audio CAS layer: shard md5s are unchanged (already opaque), but data/runs/<run>/audio/shards.json paths need to follow the rename.
- Update direct-link routes in templates (examples.html, blog_*.html, prep.html, etc.). Two viable strategies:
  (a) Add a /run/<old_name> -> /run/<opaque_id> permanent redirect table, populated from the rename mapping. Old links keep working forever.
  (b) Update every template to use the opaque id. Old git history breaks; new content is correct.
  Probably (a) — preserves outbound link integrity from blog posts and external citations.
- Build a migration that produces a one-time mapping {old_name: new_opaque_id} and applies it transactionally across:
  - data/runs/<dir> renames
  - DB rows in episode/script_version/hostprep_version/audio_artifact
  - data/runs/<run>/run_manifest.json (if it embeds the run id)
  - data/runs/<run>/config.json
  - data/runs/<run>/audio/shards.json
  - .beads/issues.jsonl (issue descriptions reference run names, e.g. oks3 talked about wh_trn_literary)
- Add a check (test or pre-commit hook) that fails if any new run dir under data/runs/ matches the legacy {novel}_{pipeline}_{panel}... shape.

Why this is a separate issue from g3hj:
- g3hj makes the axis store exist; runs can have opaque ids assigned alongside readable names, with no rename required. The webapp queries the axis store; the names happen to still be readable for human convenience.
- Without this issue, the readable names persist on disk and as the canonical key. Any new code that needs to know what a run "is" might still grep the name because it's right there. The temptation must be physically removed.
- This is destructive (renames affect git history, external links, blog content). Worth doing deliberately, not as a side-effect of g3hj.

Sequencing: do not start until g3hj is done AND the webapp has been demonstrated to work end-to-end via axis queries (i.e. a test passes asserting that renaming all runs to UUIDs in a scratch checkout doesn't break /tracker/versions, /listen/<novel>/<panel>, or audio playback).
acceptance_criteria:
- All directories under data/runs/ have opaque names (regex-checked: no name is parseable by enrichment.axes.parse_run_dir_name without raising ValueError).
- The DB stores opaque ids as the canonical key; display_label is a separate free-text field.
- Old direct links like /player?run=bh_trn_literary_hostprep continue to resolve via redirect (or all such links in repo content are updated, depending on the chosen strategy).
- A repo-wide grep for axis-token substrings (\\b(trn|emb|nop|rag)\\b, \\bhostprep\\b, \\bliterary\\b/\\balternatives\\b/\\binterdisciplinary\\b inside paths under data/runs/) returns zero hits.
- A pre-commit check or CI rule fails any future run dir whose name looks parseable.
- The blog posts and examples.html still play their referenced runs via redirects (verified end-to-end with a quick playwright/curl pass).
notes: Filed 2026-05-09. User's framing: 'we will need to explicitly refactor to replace the readable X_Y_Z run names with deliberately non-readable ids, both in the indices and on disk, removing the possibility of old bad habits coming back.' This is the enforcement leg of the two-phase plan; g3hj is the design leg.

title: Axis store: opaque IDs + (axis, value) -> {id} inverted index; arbitrary axis queries; N-axis extensibility
description:
Reframe the run-identity model. Today a run's identity and its classification are conflated in the run name (wh_trn_literary_short encodes novel+pipeline+panel+length). This lures callers into parsing the name instead of querying axes, and adding a new axis means edits across enrichment.axes.RunAxes, run_dir_name, parse_run_dir_name, the SQL schema, every webapp filter, and the dockerfile-style enumerations.

Target model: identity is opaque, classification is by axes.

  axis :: name + set of possible values
  artefact :: opaque id (UUID / content hash / nanoid — the choice matters less than the opacity)
  classification :: relation (artefact_id, axis_name, axis_value)

  forward:  id -> {axis_name: axis_value, ...}
  reverse:  (axis_name, axis_value) -> {id, ...}

  query(axes={'novel': 'wh', 'pipeline': 'transport'}) -> set[id]    # AND across axes
  query(axes={'novel': {'wh', 'bh'}})                  -> set[id]    # OR within an axis
  multi_axis intersect/union/difference: trivially set ops on the reverse-index sets.

Adding an axis becomes one declaration (axis name + value vocabulary) and one classification entry per existing artefact (or default-unspecified). No schema migration, no filter rewrites in the webapp.

Run names can persist as human-facing labels, but no machine path may parse them. Everything that today does `run_id.split('_')`, `'_hostprep' in name`, `pipeline != 'trn'`, etc. instead does `axes_for(id)['hostprep'] == True`, `'transport' in axes_for(id)['pipeline']`, etc.

This is the architectural fix for the symptom captured in BleakHouse-0wn7. 0wn7 stays valid as the narrower 'webapp uses the single source' cleanup; this issue is the redesign of what that single source is.

Open design questions (do not block filing this issue):
- ID scheme: UUID v7 (sortable, opaque), content hash (deterministic, dedup-friendly), or nanoid (short, opaque). Whatever it is, the run dir name on disk must NOT be the id.
- Axis declaration format: Python registry (one Axis instance per axis), TOML/YAML config, or DB-driven (axes themselves are rows in a table). DB-driven is most extensible but adds a query hop; Python registry is simplest and matches today's enrichment.axes shape.
- Backward compatibility: run dir names like 'wh_trn_literary_short' should keep working for the next year of git history. Solution probably: keep the dir name → axes parser as a one-way bootstrap importer, and new artefacts get opaque ids assigned at creation time. Old runs get ids retroactively from a migration that reads their config.json axes block.
- Storage: SQLite is already the experiments ledger; the inverted index is just a (artefact_id, axis_name, axis_value) table with two compound indexes. Or persist as JSON if SQLite feels heavy. Probably SQLite — already in use, and the filtering lives in db_views anyway.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new axis can be added by editing exactly one declaration (Python registry or config file). No webapp file changes required for the new axis to be queryable.
- A query API exists: query(axes_dict) -> set[id], and axes_for(id) -> dict. Both are the only machine paths used by webapp filters and CLI tools.
- No code under webapp/ or enrichment/ infers any axis from a run-id string. Grep for split('_'), endswith, startswith, '_hostprep' in name returns no axis-inference hits.
- All existing runs (the ~225 in data/runs/) have axis classifications stored and queryable, regardless of their dir name shape.
- A test asserts that adding a hypothetical axis (e.g. 'render_engine') with two values is a one-declaration change and that query({'render_engine': 'gemini'}) works without webapp edits.
notes: Filed 2026-05-09 from a design conversation grounded in the WH onboarding aftermath. User's framing: 'arbitrary queries are possible over axes and everything bottoms out in sets of ids, then ids can be used to access the data. Currently, the load which I want to be carried by opaque ids is carried by non-opaque run names, which tends to lure us into shortcuts.'
close_reason: Done (2026-05-09): axis store with opaque IDs landed in commit d8f5e477 (Stage A). Adding a new axis is one declaration in enrichment.axes.AXES; query() and axes_for() are the public API; all 222 runs have axis classifications stored and queryable; test_adding_a_hypothetical_axis_works_without_table_changes verifies extensibility.

title: Retire filename-convention inference in webapp; canonicalise axis representations
description:
The webapp infers axes from run-directory names and ships two competing axis representations (short codes like 'trn' and full words like 'transport') in the same DB column. Filter logic uses one shape; new runs land in the other. WH onboarding (oks3) hit this: the wh_trn_literary_short run lands with novel='wuthering_heights', pipeline='transport', but webapp/app.py:1419 filters with `r["pipeline"] != "trn"`, so WH disappears from /tracker/versions despite being a perfectly valid trn/literary/hostprep episode. Old runs land with novel='bh', pipeline='trn' and pass the filter. Symptom is "new runs invisible in tracker"; cause is filename-convention shorthand bleeding into the data model.

Documented intent already opposes this: webapp/run_tracker.py:8-10 says "Cell tooltips show every axis explicitly so panel/novel/hostprep/generator are never inferred from the name at display time." The implementation drifted.

Concrete known offenders to fix:
- webapp/app.py:196 — `"_hostprep" in run_dir.name` as a fallback hostprep detector
- webapp/app.py:1419-1424 — filter compares against short-code 'trn' and short-key novel ids; WH lands with full-word 'transport' and 'wuthering_heights'
- webapp/templates/metrics.html:70 — JS `c.name.includes('_hostprep')`
- enrichment/expdb scan path: emits short codes ('trn', 'bh') for some runs and full words ('transport', 'wuthering_heights') for others. Pick one shape (the full canonical axes form) and migrate the DB.

Adjacent dead-code cleanup that surfaced in the same investigation:
- /api/all-runs has zero callers; route + the all_runs half of webapp/app.py:_build_run_lists_from_db can be deleted.
- /api/novels filters on s["has_report"] from _summarize_run_dir, but report.html was untracked from git in commit 298bdbcf. Drop the has_report check or accept that /api/novels only ever shows runs with on-disk report.html. (Webapp landing page uses /tracker/versions, so /api/novels matters only for the legacy /player picker and direct /api consumers.)
acceptance_criteria:
- /tracker/versions surfaces WH (wh_trn_literary_short) without renaming the run
- No code path in webapp/ infers any axis from a run-directory string (grep for `run_id.split`, `run_id.endswith`, `_hostprep` in name, `startswith` on run names returns no axis-inference hits in webapp/* and webapp/static/*)
- Single canonical axis representation in the experiments.db `episode` table (one shape per axis: pipeline is one of {transport, embedding, no_passages, rag, random}, novel is the full canonical key)
- Existing direct links like /player?run=bh_trn_literary_hostprep continue to resolve (the run-id string itself can stay as-is; only the inferred-axis paths must go)
- /api/all-runs is removed (dead code) OR documented and kept; pick one
notes: Discovered while resuming the WH onboarding (oks3) on 2026-05-08. The deploy to fly succeeded but WH didn't appear in /tracker/versions despite having full audio. Root cause traced to db_views.matrix_rows() returning pipeline='transport' for the new run while the consuming filter at webapp/app.py:1419 hardcodes 'trn'. See conversation thread on resume of oks3.
close_reason: Done (2026-05-09): co-landing with g3hj. Single canonical axis representation in episode table (pipeline ∈ {transport, embedding, no_passages, rag}, novel = full ids). All webapp/ short-code literals replaced with axes.PIPELINE_* named constants imported from the registry. _hostprep substring check at app.py:196 dropped (returns honest 'unknown' instead of guessing). NOVEL_BY_KEY usages switched to NOVEL_BY_ID. /api/all-runs route removed (zero callers). has_report filter dropped from /api/novels (report.html stopped being tracked, filter emptied the route). WH now visible in /tracker/versions, the original motivating bug. player.js short-code refactor filed as BleakHouse-c6ls.

title: meta: persist beads state into git so issue tree survives clone
description:
The current setup loses the entire bd issue history on clone. Two layered problems:

(a) .git/info/exclude (a per-clone, never-committed gitignore) line 9 has '.beads/'. Every bd write logs 'auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1' because git refuses to track the auto-exported .beads/issues.jsonl. Likely added during an early bd init.

(b) .beads/issues.jsonl has never been committed. Every issue (including the e9go closed history and the new BleakHouse-73lo Linux migration epic) lives ONLY in .beads/dolt/issues.db on this Mac. Cloning to a Linux box → empty issue tree.

Fix:
1. Edit .git/info/exclude to drop the '.beads/' line (per-clone change; survives nothing else)
2. Update .beads/.gitignore to also exclude: backup/, .beads-credential-key, .local_version, .jsonl.lock, *.sock*, .exclusive-lock (in addition to the dolt/ + bd.sock entries it already has)
3. git add .beads/issues.jsonl + .beads/README.md + .beads/.gitignore
4. Commit + push
5. Verify the next 'bd update / bd close' completes WITHOUT the 'auto-export: git add failed' warning

Acceptance:
- A fresh clone of cbrew/BleakHouse on a different machine, after bd init/import or auto-restore, has the same open + closed issue tree (incl. BleakHouse-73lo and the e9go history)
- 'bd update <any> --notes hello' on the Mac succeeds with no auto-export warning
- .beads/dolt/ and .beads/backup/ remain untracked (binary DB shouldn't go in git)

Blocker on BleakHouse-73lo (Linux migration epic): without this, the first sub-issue (gtz8 'linux: bring up box') would clone an empty bd tree.
notes: Verifying auto-export now works with .git/info/exclude fixed.
close_reason: Done. Three changes: (1) removed '.beads/' from .git/info/exclude (a per-clone gitignore originally added by 'bd init --stealth' that hid the entire dir from git — caused the persistent 'auto-export: git add failed' warning on every bd write). (2) Committed .beads/{issues.jsonl, README.md, .gitignore, config.yaml, metadata.json, hooks/*}. .beads/.gitignore already excludes the right things (dolt/, runtime sockets, locks, credential key, backup/, sync state, ephemeral SQLite). (3) Added 'bd hooks install' as step 5/6 in scripts/bootstrap.sh — sets git config core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks/ which is per-clone and not committed by git, so every clone re-runs it. Verified: 'bd update --notes ...' now completes without the auto-export warning. Linux clone path: git clone → bash scripts/bootstrap.sh → bd hooks install runs → core.hooksPath set → bd auto-imports .beads/issues.jsonl into local Dolt → full issue tree (incl. e9go closed history + BleakHouse-73lo Linux migration epic) appears.

description:
