title: Separate user-facing run names from storage dir names
description:
The mnemonic run-dir naming pattern (bh_trn_literary_hostprep, bh_trn_literary_hostprep_short, …) has slowly become an ID system by accident.

The encoding originated as a storage convenience: name a directory after the axes that produced it so the layout is self-describing on disk. That's still a fine convention for storage. The problem is leakage into user-facing surfaces:

- Demo URLs like /report/bh_trn_literary_hostprep — the URL is the dir name.
- /listen/<novel>/<panel> insulates the consumer site, but most scholar URLs (matrix popover, /api/runs/{run_id}/manifest, /api/runs/{run_id}/prep, /script/{run_id}) take the dir name verbatim.
- Code that wants to ask 'is this a short variant?' reaches for substring matching on the dir name. The proper answer is parse_run_dir_name(run_id).length == 'short' (the parser owns the encoding, callers see the decoded axis), but the lure is to write run_id.endswith('_short') and move on.

What we actually want is two things:
1. A storage path: opaque if necessary (UUID, content hash, or the current mnemonic — doesn't matter so long as nothing user-facing reads it).
2. A user-facing label: a short stable string the reader sees in URLs and UIs. Could be derived from axes ('Bleak House — literary panel — host-prepared, short cut') or a researcher-supplied nickname.

## Why this isn't urgent

The current setup works. Mnemonic dir names are tolerable because we have one developer who knows the encoding and the leakage hasn't bitten on production. But:
- It tempts callers into substring-matching code that breaks when the encoding evolves (we just added _short — adding 'long' explicitly someday would break naive parsers).
- If we ever want to rename a run for clarity or migrate to opaque storage, every caller that reads dir names directly is a touchpoint.

## Migration shape (sketch — refine when picked up)

1. Episode table already has separate label column (current dir name) and the underlying axes (novel, panel, pipeline, hostprep, generator, ref_tools, length). Add a display_label column and populate from a deterministic axis-formatter.
2. Webapp endpoints accept either the storage label or the display label, with display preferred for URL canonicalization.
3. Templates and matrix popovers source from display_label, never from the dir name.
4. parse_run_dir_name remains the only callsite that reads encoded dir names — and it's only used by the experiments scanner that scans data/runs.
5. Audit: grep for 'run_id', 'run.label', 'endswith("_short")', 'endswith("_hostprep")', etc. — every leaky callsite gets fixed to use the decoded axes or the display label.

## Sequencing

Comes AFTER the length-axis epic (BleakHouse-x3r6) ships. Adding _short to dir names extends the existing pattern; this task changes the pattern itself. Doing them simultaneously would change two layers at once.

description:
Render ~30-min short variants of every (novel, panel, pipeline, hostprep) cell so the consumer site can default to a digestible cut. Long-form stays as a sibling for the scholar matrix (research/comparison value).

## Decisions

- New axis: length ∈ {long, short}. Run-name suffix '_short' for the short variant; bare base name remains the long-form default. Same convention as '_hostprep'.
- Sibling run dirs: <base>_short/ alongside <base>/. Each variant has its own phase3_episode.json, audio render, and shards. Most principled — matches how generator/hostprep already extend.
- Scholar matrix collapse: existing cell (novel, panel, pipeline, hostprep) keeps its place; popover surfaces both lengths with separate play links. Cell count unchanged.
- Consumer site: default to short. Card shows a 'longer cut' link to the long version when one exists.
- New shorts use the SHARDS renderer (enrichment.render_audio.render_episode_to_shards) from the outset. No legacy monolithic mp3 + no forced-alignment step. The forced-alignment work shipped in BleakHouse-kqzp was specifically for the existing long-form mp3s; new content writes shards directly.

## Why this and not 'replace longs'

The forced-alignment migration we shipped in BleakHouse-kqzp added value to the existing long-form runs. Throwing them away discards work + the experimental matrix's research story. Generating shorts alongside is cheap (~$30 TTS for 32 cells, ~5 min Phase 3 per cell, ~10 min TTS per cell, ~2 GB additional R2). Decide later whether to keep populating both axes for new novels.

## Cost / effort (revised)

- Phase 3 regen with shorter target: ~5 min Sonnet per cell.
- TTS Phase 4 (shards renderer): ~10 min per cell × 32 ≈ ~5 hours.
- DVC add + push: ~2 GB upload.
- Total wall clock: ~5-6 hours, no overnight forced-alignment pass.

## Sub-tasks

See sub-issues — 8 tasks from axis change through deploy. (Original task 5 'forced-align all 32 shorts' was closed as not needed; the shards renderer eliminates that step.)

title: Migrate off DVC to a small content-addressed store (CAS)
description:
DVC was a defensible early choice (git-for-data with pipelines, multi-developer sync) but doesn't fit this project's current shape:

- One developer day-to-day; cross-machine sync is rarely exercised.
- The pipeline doesn't run through DVC's executor — we have shell scripts and a Burr state machine, and dvc.yaml stages are mostly artifacts.
- Deployment talks to R2 directly (302 redirects from the webapp); DVC plays no runtime role.
- Most run-dir files are JSON small enough to live in git directly; only audio mp3s are genuinely large.

The friction it adds is concrete and recurring:

- Symlink-as-source-of-truth complicates code. We patched _resolve_path in webapp/db_views.py because absolute Mac-local DVC paths leaked through into hostprep_version DB rows and broke /api/runs/X/prep on Fly.
- dvc unprotect required before any write to a DVC-tracked file (data/experiments.db hits this regularly).
- dvc.lock churns from unrelated stages; CLAUDE.md gotchas list documents 'git checkout -- dvc.lock' as a workaround before staging feature commits.
- dvc pull -r r2 deletes tracked files for removed stages, which is why deploy_demo.sh has a comment saying 'deliberately do NOT run dvc pull here'.
- DVC cache symlinks have pointed at /Volumes/Crucial X9; an unplugged external drive can disappear half the working tree.

What we actually need from the storage layer is much smaller:
  cas.put(path) -> md5
  cas.url(md5) -> R2 URL
  cas.local_path(md5) -> Path | None

A ~50-line module replacing dvc add / dvc pull / dvc push for our actual usage. Manifests (shards.json, run_manifest.json, etc.) reference bytes by md5; canonical bytes live at data/blobs/<md5[:2]>/<md5[2:]> locally and at the matching path on R2. The webapp's audio routes already use this content-addressed pattern; CAS makes the rest of the codebase consistent with it.

## Migration shape

1. Build webapp/cas.py (or tools/cas/) implementing put/url/local_path/push. R2 upload via boto3 or rclone shell-out.
2. Walk every .dvc sidecar; build a mapping (tracked_path -> md5). Inventory which paths are referenced by code/manifests vs. orphans.
3. Update manifests that reference paths to reference md5s instead. Specifically: shards.json (already md5-keyed); audio_manifest.json (refs path); the dvc.lock-derived _AUDIO_R2_URLS map in webapp/app.py.
4. Replace symlinks-into-.dvc-cache with regular files at data/blobs/<md5> (or keep symlinks under our own non-DVC layout — choose during design).
5. Update scripts/deploy_demo.sh to push new mp3s via 'cas push' instead of 'dvc push'.
6. Delete .dvc files, dvc.lock, dvc.yaml; remove dvc + boto3-via-dvc deps from pyproject.toml; verify a fresh clone + 'cas pull' reconstructs the working tree.
7. Update CLAUDE.md: drop the 'dvc unprotect' / 'git checkout -- dvc.lock' gotchas; add the new CAS workflow.

## Additional requirement: kill silent file-existence fallbacks (added 2026-05-07)

The bleak_house passage-text bug shipped a silent-fallback pattern that this migration is the right place to eliminate. Concrete failure: enrichment/segment_transport.py:build_passage_assignments had

    if novel and novel != 'bleak_house':
        enr_path = DATA_DIR / 'novels' / novel / 'passages_enriched.json'
    else:
        enr_path = DATA_DIR / 'passages_enriched.json'    # legacy path, no longer exists
    if enr_path.exists():
        with open(enr_path) as f:
            enrichment_data = json.load(f)
    # enrichment_data stays None when the path is missing → enr_map empty → every
    # passage's text/summary/best_quote is the empty string. No exception, no
    # warning. The 32 long-form runs masked it for months because their
    # phase1_assignments.json was a snapshot from before bleak_house moved under
    # data/novels/. New bleak_house runs silently produced empty passage texts.

This is exactly what CLAUDE.md's 'don't do fallback options, try harder to get things right' rule is supposed to prevent, but the policy is not enforced anywhere.

The CAS migration is the natural place to fix this because it is already consolidating path resolution. Required additions to the migration:

1. Replace 'if path.exists()' + silent default with direct open() (let FileNotFoundError propagate) wherever the data is required for correctness. Audit pass: grep the codebase for 'if .*\.exists\(\)' followed by skip/None/[]/{} fallback. For each hit, decide: is this data optional, or required? If required, raise.

2. Centralise path resolution into named helpers under cas/ (e.g. cas.enrichment_path_for(novel) -> Path, cas.assignments_path_for(run_id) -> Path). Each helper raises FileNotFoundError on miss with a contextual message. No caller resolves paths bespoke. The bleak_house special case existed only because path resolution was duplicated; consolidating the helper eliminates the class.

3. Delete every legacy-layout reference encountered along the way:
   - data / 'passages_enriched.json' (singular root) — replaced by data/novels/<id>/passages_enriched.json
   - any 'if novel == "bleak_house"' special case that survives from before the layout moved
   - any reference to a path that no longer exists, even if the surrounding code 'works' because of a fallback

4. Add a smoke-test that runs at pipeline start: for the active novel, the standard enrichment fields (text, summary, best_quote) must be non-empty for ≥95% of passages. Catches the broader 'data is loadable but unusable' class.

The fix already shipped for the bleak_house immediate site (segment_transport.py:112-122 now reads BLEAKHOUSE_NOVEL with default 'bleak_house' and uses data/novels/<novel>/passages_enriched.json directly, with no .exists() guard). That fix is a band-aid; the audit and centralisation are the proper resolution and belong in this migration.

## Scope / non-goals

- In scope: replace the DVC + R2 storage layer with a single small CAS module that addresses bytes by md5. End state: zero .dvc files, zero references to the dvc CLI in scripts.
- In scope: silent-fallback audit + centralised path-helper consolidation (see 'Additional requirement' above).
- Out of scope: changing R2 itself (we keep the same bucket and md5-content-addressed path scheme — bytes already live at /files/md5/<prefix>/<rest>). Existing R2 contents are reused as-is.
- Out of scope: changing the webapp's audio routes' shape. They already serve by md5; CAS just provides a clean local_path/url pair to consult.

## Why this is forward-compatible with current work

The forced-alignment migration's audio-routing fix (BleakHouse-kqzp) uses .dvc/cache/files/md5/<prefix>/<rest> as the local cache path. Under CAS, that line becomes cas.local_path(md5). Same shape, one line of code change. Nothing about the forced-alignment migration locks us into DVC.

## Cost / payoff

Cost: ~1-2 days careful work for the storage swap; +0.5 day for the silent-fallback audit + helper consolidation. The mechanical parts (walk .dvc, compute mappings, update manifests) are straightforward; the careful part is verifying that a fresh clone + cas pull reconstructs everything currently reachable through dvc pull -r r2. Need a test that runs in a clean checkout.

Payoff: absolute-path bug class disappears (no more symlinks pointing to host-specific paths); route code simplifies; dvc.lock churn ends; deploy scripts no longer have 'deliberately do NOT run dvc pull' comments; one fewer tool in the stack. Plus: the entire silent-fallback-on-missing-data bug class disappears — when data is missing, the pipeline fails loudly instead of producing empty passage popovers months later.

## Sequencing

Do this AFTER BleakHouse-kqzp (forced-alignment migration) lands. Reasons:
- That migration is mid-flight; introducing infra change underneath would compound risk.
- Forced-alignment will exercise the existing DVC + R2 path one more time (dvc add + dvc push for the new shards). Smoother to ship that migration, validate the demo, then refactor the storage layer with no other moving parts.

When picking this up: scope it as its own epic with sub-tasks (design + module / inventory / migrate manifests / update webapp / update deploy / delete DVC / silent-fallback audit / path-helper consolidation / smoke-test fresh clone). Don't try to do it as a single bd issue — it's at least 5-6 hours of mechanical migration plus verification, plus the audit pass.

title: Forced-align rendered mp3s to rebuild per-turn timing in manifest.json
description:
Click-to-jump in the audio player lands on the wrong turn because the served manifest's per-turn start_ms/end_ms are built from a 15-chars/sec character-count estimate, not from the actual rendered mp3. Drift is per-turn, varies with character count, and reaches ~10 minutes by the end of a 100-minute episode.

Rebuilding from the TTS cache only fully measures 2 of 32 audio runs (bh_trn_alternatives_hostprep, bh_trn_literary_hostprep); the other 30 have partial caches and would still need char-estimates for missing turns.

Plan: forced-align each rendered podcast.mp3 against its phase3_episode.json transcript (whisperx, montreal-forced-aligner, or similar). Write the aligned per-turn timestamps into data/runs/<run>/audio/manifest.json. The webapp already prefers audio/manifest.json over the run-level manifest when present (webapp/app.py get_manifest), so no webapp changes needed once the files exist.

Affects: every legacy single-mp3 run. The shards-mode runs are unaffected (they don't use ms offsets — turn boundaries are structural shard boundaries).
close_reason: Done (2026-05-09 review): tools/forced_align/ tooling shipped; 32 data/runs/<run>/audio/manifest.json files exist (matches the 32 legacy single-mp3 runs the issue identified). Per-turn start_ms/end_ms are populated; webapp prefers audio/manifest.json over the run-level manifest as designed.

title: webapp audio resolution: deploy-time global index from dvc.lock (eliminate run_manifest staleness)
description:
Replace the run_manifest.json-based audio-hash lookup with a deploy-time global index built directly from dvc.lock — the actual source of truth. Eliminates the silent staleness bug where re-rendered audio gets a new dvc.lock hash but run_manifest.json never refreshes (because the run_manifest dvc.yaml stage doesn't list dvc.lock as a dep), so the webapp keeps serving the old hash and R2 404s.

CURRENT ARCHITECTURE (fragile)
  dvc.lock                                   ← canonical hash source
    ↓ generate_run_manifest.py (manual; not triggered by dvc.lock changes)
  data/runs/<id>/run_manifest.json           ← derived cache; can drift
    ↓ webapp/_load_run_manifest()
  R2 URL: <R2_PUBLIC>/files/md5/<h[:2]>/<h[2:]>

PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE
  dvc.lock                                   ← canonical hash source
    ↓ scripts/build_audio_index.py (run by stage_demo.sh + as a pre-commit hook)
  data/audio_index.json                      ← single global file, all runs × variants
    ↓ webapp reads at request time
  R2 URL: <R2_PUBLIC>/files/md5/<h[:2]>/<h[2:]>

WORK
  1. New scripts/build_audio_index.py: reads dvc.lock, emits data/audio_index.json mapping (run_id, variant_name) → {hash, audio_file, audio_manifest, stage}. Idempotent. Fast (~ms for 1,700 stages).
  2. dvc.yaml: declare new stage audio_index that depends on dvc.lock and outs data/audio_index.json (cache:false — it's small + needed in fresh clones).
  3. webapp/app.py:
     - New _load_audio_index() reading data/audio_index.json once at startup (cache in memory; reload on file mtime change).
     - Refactor /audio/<id>/<file> handler to use the global index.
     - Strip audio_variants reads from _load_run_manifest() — that field stays in run_manifest.json for backward compat / human inspection but the webapp no longer depends on it for URL resolution.
  4. scripts/stage_demo.sh: invoke build_audio_index.py before the copy loop so the demo image always ships a current index.
  5. .pre-commit-config.yaml: add a hook that regenerates audio_index.json if dvc.lock changed in the staged diff. Catches staleness at commit time rather than at deploy time.
  6. tests/test_audio_index_consistency.py: assert every audio-variant hash in audio_index.json matches its dvc.lock entry. Catches future drift.
  7. docs/dvc.md: document the new mechanism + retire the 'audio_variants in run_manifest' description.

ACCEPTANCE
  - data/audio_index.json exists, regenerable, listed as a dvc.yaml stage with dvc.lock as a dep.
  - Webapp's /audio resolution uses the global index; no longer reads audio_variants from run_manifest.
  - Pre-commit hook prevents committing a stale index.
  - Test passes locally and the staleness bug is no longer reachable.
  - docs/dvc.md reflects the new flow.

WHY THIS IS ENTANGLED WITH THE MIGRATION (BleakHouse-1dnv)
  The migration moved ~14 stages × ~217 instances of JSON outs into DVC's
  cache:true. Every dvc commit on those stages updates dvc.lock. Pre-
  migration, only audio re-renders mutated dvc.lock; post-migration, any
  pipeline-output regen does. So the run_manifest staleness window —
  previously narrow — is now wide-open whenever any DVC-managed output
  refreshes. Phase 4 (BleakHouse-x5a3) is the migration's workflow-
  finalisation step; the new-run convention it documents has to include
  this index regen, or it ships an actively-broken deploy path.
close_reason: Superseded by the bake-at-build deploy redesign (live https://bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev/tracker, machine 48e063db3e4918, image 680 MB). dvc-pull-at-startup approach was tried first and pivoted away from due to cold-start time and dvc-pull-deletes-orphans behavior on a 1-vCPU 1GB Fly machine. Final architecture: deploy_demo.sh tar -ch's the dvc-pulled JSON tree (165 MB; symlinks dereferenced), Containerfile COPY+untars at build, container has no DVC binary / no R2 secrets / no volume. Webapp 302-redirects audio mp3s to R2 using URLs built from dvc.lock at startup (39 URLs loaded; verified 302 + 206 byte stream from R2).

title: DVC migration: lock retrofit dirs from dvc repro (frozen stages)
description:
Follow-up to BleakHouse-ddxi. After Phase 0 added retrofit dirs to runs_by_id (so DVC can hash their outputs), retrofit phase3_episode.json files are now reachable by 'dvc repro' — which would invoke today's pipeline code against the retrofit's frozen phase2_plan.json and overwrite the snapshot with fresh LLM responses. That defeats the point of a retrofit (preserved record of pipeline output at a specific date).

Risk is latent today: 'dvc repro' is rarely invoked by hand in the current workflow; the migration uses 'dvc commit' (records on-disk hash without re-running). But Phase 4 (BleakHouse-x5a3) establishes the new-run convention which is likely to normalise 'dvc repro'.

Plan:
  1. Detect retrofits via run_manifest.json's 'retrofit_of' field (cleanest signal — already used by generate_runs_yaml.py's axes fallback).
  2. In scripts/generate_runs_yaml.py, split runs_by_id into runs_by_id_canonical (non-retrofit) and runs_by_id_retrofit. Same for the run_ids_* lists (run_ids_phase3_canonical, etc.). Keep runs_by_id as the union for callers that don't care.
  3. In dvc.yaml, change existing per-phase foreach references to iterate over the *_canonical variants — same coverage as today (retrofits weren't visible before Phase 0).
  4. Add new frozen stages (e.g. phase3_episode_retrofit) iterating the *_retrofit variants with 'frozen: true'. Outputs hit the same file paths so DVC tracks the hash, but 'dvc repro' skips them.
  5. Verify: 'dvc repro phase3_episode' covers all canonical runs, ignores retrofits. 'dvc repro phase3_episode_retrofit' is a no-op (frozen).

Acceptance: 'dvc repro' against a retrofit's phase3_episode never invokes the regenerator; retrofit outputs still appear in 'dvc status' / dvc.lock with their hashes; canonical run coverage unchanged from before this ticket.
close_reason: Superseded by the bake-at-build deploy redesign (live https://bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev/tracker, machine 48e063db3e4918, image 680 MB). dvc-pull-at-startup approach was tried first and pivoted away from due to cold-start time and dvc-pull-deletes-orphans behavior on a 1-vCPU 1GB Fly machine. Final architecture: deploy_demo.sh tar -ch's the dvc-pulled JSON tree (165 MB; symlinks dereferenced), Containerfile COPY+untars at build, container has no DVC binary / no R2 secrets / no volume. Webapp 302-redirects audio mp3s to R2 using URLs built from dvc.lock at startup (39 URLs loaded; verified 302 + 206 byte stream from R2).

title: Migrate all pipeline-output JSON to DVC (proper data/code separation)
description:
Migrate the pipeline's JSON outputs from git to DVC. Today the repo muddles the two: program-generated JSON sits as text in git while binary audio lives correctly in DVC + R2. A clean clone pulls ~350 MB of pipeline outputs that should be content-hashed in remote storage. This ticket captures the full migration end-to-end (declarations, on-disk reconciliation, R2 push, gitignore, history rewrite, tests, docs) so a future session can pick it up without prior context.

PRINCIPLE
  git: source code, configs, pipeline definitions, hand-curated small inputs.
       Everything in git is human-authored.
  DVC: program-generated outputs. Versioned by content hash. Tracked via
       'outs:' entries in dvc.yaml stages; actual blobs in R2.
  Clean clone + 'dvc pull' must reconstruct everything needed to inspect
  or re-run any version of the pipeline.

WHY THIS ISN'T A ONE-LINE FIX
  The dvc.yaml DOES already define stages with foreach over runs.yaml,
  and those stages declare 'outs:'. The bug is that 16 of those outs
  carry 'cache: false' — explicitly opting out of the DVC cache and
  parking the JSON in git. Flipping those alone is small. But three
  other gaps make the migration bigger:

    A. Eight output types have NO outs declaration anywhere (mostly
       the recorder sidecars added 2026-05-02 and Cerebras-only files).
    B. runs.yaml is stale (217 dirs on disk, 194 listed; rwv-audio not
       in run_ids_audio).
    C. report.html / report.txt are simultaneously declared as outs in
       dvc.yaml AND gitignored as of 2026-05-02 commit 298bdbc — the
       conflict has to be resolved before flipping cache.

    run_manifest.json                 small public index for tracker

    phase2_plan.json                       616     phase2_plan        yes
    embedding_artifacts.json                80     [MISSING]          —

    phase2_5_host_briefs.json              171     phase2_5           yes
    phase2_5_reading_list.json              58     phase2_5_reading_list yes
    phase2_5_timings.json                   15     [MISSING]          —
    phase3_episode.json                    609     phase3_episode     yes
    phase3_timings.json                      1     [MISSING]          —
    phase3_generation_metrics.json           6     [MISSING]          —
    phase3_teaser.json                      22     [MISSING]          —
    manifest.json (legacy + audio)         641     phase4_post / run_manifest yes
    manifest_qwen.json                       4     phase4_audio_qwen  yes
    manifest_trevelyan_v2.json               3     phase4_audio_trevelyan_v2 yes
    shards.json                              1     [MISSING]          —
    quote_verification.json                547     quote_verification yes
    phase_timings.json                     216     [MISSING]          —
    run_timings.json                         2     [MISSING]          —
                                       ─────

  Already DVC-cached (cache: true):
    audio/podcast.mp3                   32 runs    phase4_audio
    audio/podcast_qwen.mp3               4 runs    phase4_audio_qwen
    audio/podcast_trevelyan_v2.mp3       3 runs    phase4_audio_trevelyan_v2
    audio/shards/<profile>/*.mp3       120+ shards (rwv only so far)

  Already gitignored (regenerable derivatives, decision pending re. dvc.yaml):
    report.html, report.txt           webapp/build_report.py output
    experiments.db                    enrichment.expdb scan output

PLAN

PHASE 0 — Reconcile the existing infrastructure (1 day)
  a. Re-run 'uv run python -m scripts.generate_runs_yaml'; commit the
     updated runs.yaml so rwv_trn_literary_hostprep et al. enter

  b. Decide retrofit / archived-run policy: either extend the foreach
     lists in generate_runs_yaml.py (so the 23 retrofit_<timestamp>_*
     dirs join the canonical lists) OR document them as out-of-pipeline

  c. Resolve report.html/txt: drop from dvc.yaml outs of phase4_post
     (recommended — they're fully rebuildable from phase3_episode.json
     and were just gitignored 2026-05-02). The alternative (un-gitignore

       shards.json → outs of phase4_audio_trevelyan_v2 (per-profile)

title: Phase 3 prompt: target 30-min episodes (was 70-min)
description:
The phase 3 system prompt in enrichment/generate_podcast.py asks Sonnet for ~1500 words per segment, ~1800 for the opening. With 7 segments that's ~10,800 words ≈ ~70 minutes at 150 wpm. After TTS pacing (gemini-3.1-flash adds pauses for variety) the actual audio runs ~90 minutes per episode.

Empirical compliance check on rwv_trn_literary (2026-05-02): Sonnet overshoots its own target by ~9% (11,773 words vs 10,800). So the issue is the PROMPT TARGET, not Sonnet's discipline.

Cost implication: TTS dominates per-episode cost (~$2.70 of a $7 run for room_with_a_view). A 30-min episode would cut TTS spend ~3×, bringing per-episode total under $5.

PROPOSED CHANGE (to test, not to ship blindly)

In enrichment/generate_podcast.py around the **Segment length** block:

  Each segment should be approximately 1,500 words (1,800 for the opening
  segment with introductions). This is roughly 10 minutes of audio.

→ change to something like

  Each segment should be approximately 600 words (700 for the opening
  segment with introductions). This is roughly 4 minutes of audio.

  Prioritise quality over quantity ruthlessly. A 4-minute segment is
  about three substantive points well-developed, not eight points
  rushed. Drop a topic before padding it.

7 × 600 + opening ≈ 4,300 words ≈ ~30 min audio. Validate empirically:
re-render one A/B segment under each prompt and compare audio length.

OPEN QUESTIONS

(a) Is 30 min the right target, or 45? The poster/papers can present
either. 45 min × 5-6 substantive points might preserve the panel's
conversational register better than 30 min × 3 points.

(b) Does shortening per-segment word counts hurt the discussion's
depth in measurable ways (quote density, theme coverage)? An ablation
on one well-known novel (BH) would settle this.

(c) Should the 'opening' segment scale separately? Introductions are
mostly fixed-length regardless of episode length.

NOT URGENT — user explicitly said hold the change until investigated. Do not auto-apply.
acceptance_criteria: (a) one paragraph in CLAUDE.md (or papers/ design notes) records the target episode length and the rationale; (b) prompt edit committed in a single PR with before/after word-count + audio-length numbers in the commit message; (c) at least one A/B comparison render shows the new prompt actually lands in the target range (within 10%); (d) any quality-regression risk from shorter segments is either ruled out empirically or flagged for human review.
close_reason: Short-form prompt variant added (~600 words/segment vs 1500); selected via build_messages(length='short'). Long block unchanged so existing callers default to long. Plumbing into the pipeline runner via --length flag is BleakHouse-4mpi.

title: Consolidate duplicate enrichment paths into one canonical pipeline
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-02 while running the room_with_a_view bootstrap. The repo currently has FOUR enrichment paths split across two artefacts, and the duplication is a confusion vector — adding a novel means deciding whether to use the sync or batch variant for each, with no rule.

CURRENT STATE

Producing passages_enriched.json (per-passage literary features):
  A. enrichment/submit_batch.py + enrichment/collect_results.py
     — Anthropic Batch API, 50% discount, async (minutes-to-hours wall-clock).
     This is what was actually used for room_with_a_view.
  B. enrichment/test_single.py
     — sync per-chapter, single-call. Documented as 'test before batch';
     not a production path. Probably fine to keep as a debug tool.

Producing passages_contextual.json (per-passage chapter context):
  C. enrichment/generate_contexts.py
     — sync per-passage with Anthropic prompt caching on the chapter prefix.
     Already instrumented (BleakHouse-ybbn).
  D. enrichment/submit_context_batch.py + enrichment/collect_context_batch.py
     — Anthropic Batch API. The submit_context_batch docstring acknowledges:
       'Prompt caching is best-effort in batches (not guaranteed), but the
        50% batch discount on input tokens compensates.'
     So C and D have a real economic trade-off: C guarantees cache hits,
     D guarantees the batch discount but may miss cache. Pick one.

C and D are the actual duplicate; A and B are different roles.

THE PROBLEM

When a new novel needs enrichment, the choice between C and D isn't documented in any user-facing way. Both produce the same artefact. A reader of the repo can't tell which is canonical. We'd be mid-novel-bootstrap right now and would have had to pick again.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

Pick one of C or D as the official path. Decide based on actual numbers:
  - measure C and D on the same novel for total cost + wall-clock
  - the choice should be permanent — delete the other path

Then:
  - rename surviving entry to enrichment/run_passage_contexts.py (or similar)
  - delete the loser; keep test_single (B) only as a debug tool
  - document in CLAUDE.md the one-line workflow: 'a new novel ⇒ run X'
  - update dvc.yaml to reference only the canonical path

DON'T DEFER

The user explicitly called out that 'alternate paths are confusion waiting to happen' — and was right. The vo7 run we just kicked off used path A for literary enrichment but hasn't yet used C or D for contexts. Resolve before the next novel onboarding so we don't end up with three flavours when someone touches it again.
acceptance_criteria: (a) one chosen contexts path lives in the repo, the other deleted; (b) CLAUDE.md (or equivalent) documents the canonical 'add a novel' command sequence as a single linear path; (c) dvc.yaml references only the surviving stage; (d) test_single.py is either deleted or clearly comment-tagged as a debug tool only; (e) a follow-up commit verifies that running the canonical path on a fresh test novel works end-to-end.
notes:
Closed 2026-05-04 after end-to-end consolidation.

Stage 1 (enrichment-layer comparison on Oliver Twist, 3830 passages):
  Path C (sync+cache): 110 min, ~$6.27, 100% coverage
  Path D (batch):       63 min, ~$3.21, 99.87% coverage (5 transient API failures)
  Cosine median 0.987 (n=500), p10=0.903, schema match on 3825 pairs.
  Spot-checks of low-cosine pairs: paraphrase variance, not factual drift.

Stage 2 (downstream pipeline ×2, ot_trn_literary_hostprep, C-input vs D-input):
  Phase 0 segments — same number (7), different titles (LLM nondeterminism)
  Phase 1 — 53 vs 54 passages selected; C ⊂ D (one extra in D).
  Phase 2.5 reading list — 72 vs 67 entries.
  Phase 3 script — 111 vs 119 turns, 11.3K vs 11.7K words. Same panel.
  Conclusion: downstream divergence dominated by Sonnet 4.6 sampling
  noise, not contextual.json variance.

Decision: Path D wins.

Phase 4-5 (delete + rename):
  Deleted enrichment/generate_contexts.py (Path C, 200 lines).
  Deleted scripts/compare_context_paths.py (single-use scaffold).
  Renamed enrichment/submit_context_batch.py → submit_passage_contexts.py
  Renamed enrichment/collect_context_batch.py → collect_passage_contexts.py
  Renamed enrichment/submit_batch.py → submit_passages_enriched.py
  Renamed enrichment/collect_results.py → collect_passages_enriched.py
  test_single.py retained as documented structured-output sanity check.

Phase 6 (single-command onboarding + verification):
  Added scripts/add_novel.sh — idempotent end-to-end pipeline.
  Updated CLAUDE.md, docs/llm_call_sites.md, design/embedding_experiments.md.
  Verified on Mrs. Dalloway (1925 modernist; structurally different from
  Victorian calibration corpus). Required adding a 'chunked' parsing
  strategy to segment_novel.py (NovelConfig.chunk_paragraphs / start_marker
  / end_marker) for novels without conventional chapter structure.
  Mrs. Dalloway: 113 chunks × ~7 paragraphs = 786 raw → 791 enriched →
  791 contextual (782 with text) → clusters + 19 character arcs.

Rollback tag: stage12-complete-pre-deletion (at 3ed2c3d1).
Branch: consolidate-enrichment-paths (7 commits since tag).
close_reason: Consolidation complete: 4 paths → 2 (one per artefact), single-command onboarding via add_novel.sh, verified end-to-end on Mrs. Dalloway.

title: Cost/time/token instrumentation across all pipeline phases
description:
Extend the existing Recorder pattern (enrichment/timing.py) to capture per-call timing and tokens (or chars/audio-seconds for TTS) for every LLM call across phases 0/1/2/3/4. Aggregate into a top-level run_timings.json that scripts/timings_summary.py rolls up into a single per-stage cost breakdown.

Today: only phase 2.5 (host_prep) writes phase2_5_timings.json. Phases 1, 2, 3, 4 produce nothing structured. timings_summary.py only reads phase 2.5.

Sub-task ordering:
  T1. Extend timing.py with a TTS-friendly recorder (chars input, audio-seconds output) + cost rates for Gemini 2.5 flash/pro TTS.
  T2. Wrap render_audio.py (phase 4) — write phase4_timings.json to run_dir on render.
  T3. Wrap generate_podcast.py (phase 3) — write phase3_timings.json.
  T4. Wrap phase 1-2 LLM modes (embedding_podcast.py:555, design_segments.py:283).
  T5. Add scripts/build_run_timings.py that aggregates all phase*_timings.json files into run_timings.json with stage labels.
  T6. Extend timings_summary.py to read run_timings.json with per-stage breakdown and Gemini TTS pricing.

Why now: BleakHouse-vo7 (full new-novel run with cost tracking) requires this instrumentation to satisfy its acceptance criteria (e), (f), (g).
acceptance_criteria: (a) every LLM call across phases 1-4 records a CallEvent with started_at/duration_s/input_tokens/output_tokens (or chars/audio_s for TTS); (b) each phase writes phase<N>_timings.json into run_dir; (c) a single run_timings.json aggregates all phases with stage labels; (d) scripts/timings_summary.py prints per-stage and total cost in dollars from run_timings.json; (e) verified on a small partial render (mmar segment 0 or similar) — every /bin/zsh.001 spent is reflected in the report.
close_reason: all six sub-tasks shipped: T1 (timing.py TTS extensions), T2 (render_audio sidecar), T3 (generate_podcast sidecar), T4 (embedding_podcast + design_segments sidecars), T5 (run_timings.json aggregator), T6 (multi-model pricing module with verified Gemini 2.5 flash/pro and 3.1 flash TTS rates). Validated end-to-end on mmar_trn_alternatives_hostprep segment 6: 12 events, $0.157 reported.

title: Per-turn audio shards as primary audio format (Option B)
description:
Replace the (single mp3 + audio/manifest.json) pair with per-turn audio shards played as a sequential playlist. Turn boundary becomes structural (end of shard N = start of shard N+1) so timing drift between text and audio becomes physically impossible. Eliminates the dual-source-of-truth that caused the motf_trn_alternatives sync drift (mp3 was 15.7s shorter than the manifest claimed).

Decision context: chosen 2026-05-02 over the integrity-check approach (Option A) and forced-alignment approach (Option D) on the principle that future correctness > backward compatibility. See architecture discussion in 2026-05-02 session.

Scope:
- TTS pipeline emits one mp3 per turn (already partially does — phase4 produces segment_NN.mp3 shards before concatenating; preserve them as the canonical artefact instead of discarding)
- Webapp player switches sources turn-by-turn instead of seeking inside one big mp3
- Storage: shards on R2, content-addressable like the current single mp3
- DB: audio_artifact rows become per-turn (or one row + a shards manifest pointing at hashes)
- Sync logic: highlight changes on '\<audio> ended' events, not on timeupdate within a single source
- Player UX: sequential prefetch of next 1-2 shards to mask gaps; scrubbing across turns means switching <audio> src

Out of scope (cover in dependent ticket):
- Migration of existing 32 single-mp3 renders to shard form (forced-alignment based)
acceptance_criteria: (a) TTS pipeline outputs and persists per-turn mp3 shards; (b) DB schema captures shard sequence per script_version; (c) webapp player advances highlight on shard boundary events; (d) drift between rendered audio and script becomes structurally impossible (no per-turn ms offsets stored anywhere); (e) at least 2 newly rendered runs play end-to-end on bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev with no sync drift.
notes: Reference: 2026-05-02 sync-drift investigation. Drift evidence: motf_trn_alternatives manifest claims 3402958ms, ffprobe reports 3387264ms. The 30 other audio runs are within ±54ms but the architecture allows arbitrary drift to enter undetected.

title: Retire Fly volumes; serve audio from R2; move telemetry to stdout
description: With Cloudflare R2 now configured as the DVC remote and 38 audio mp3s (3.70 GB) durably stored there, the Fly volumes' two roles (audio cache + telemetry append-files) can be eliminated. R2 becomes the single source of truth for audio; telemetry stops needing persistent storage at all. Fly machines become stateless app servers. Saves ~$9.60/mo plus the architectural simplification: no two-volume divergence, no dvc-pull at deploy, smaller container, dev/staging/prod parity.
acceptance_criteria: (a) /audio/<id>/<file> returns 302 to a working R2 URL; range scrubbing works; (b) /api/feedback and /api/pageview log to stdout (visible in 'fly logs') without writing to any volume; (c) fly.toml has no [mounts] block; (d) Fly machines start clean from a stateless image; (e) audio plays end-to-end on bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev; (f) volumes destroyed.
notes: Step 5 deploy complete on 2026-05-02. Two bugs found and fixed in deploy/c0f21b9: (1) stage_demo.sh missing run_manifest.json, (2) webapp missing logging.basicConfig. Existing fly machines had to be destroyed (--force, both stopped) to detach volumes — fly deploy --yes does not bypass the volume-config-drift warning. Two unattached audio_data volumes remain on the app and are scheduled for destruction in step 6 after soak. Live: https://bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev/ — /tracker 200, audio 302→R2 with range, /api/pageview JSON to stdout in fly logs.

title: Make audio path config-driven for Mac→Linux migration
description: The webapp resolves /audio/{run_id}/{filename} by following filesystem symlinks under data/runs/<run>/audio/, which point absolutely to /Volumes/Crucial X9/bleakhouse_audio/dvc-cache/files/md5/. That works on Mac (the 3.9 GB DVC cache lives on an external SSD at that path) and on Fly (stage_demo.sh rewrites the symlinks to /app/audio_volume at staging time). It will break on the upcoming Linux dev box: the path doesn't exist, and the symlinks have no fallback resolution. Make audio resolution config-driven so moving the cache is a config change, not a code change.
acceptance_criteria: (a) BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT env var documented and read by serve_audio; (b) webapp serves audio on a fresh Linux box with the cache mounted at any path, no symlink rewriting required; (c) Fly deploy still works (audio smoke test passes); (d) Mac dev box keeps working (env var defaults are sensible).
notes:
Existing data already has the lever we need: every audio variant in run_manifest.json carries its dvc_hash. We can resolve (run_id, filename) → cache blob without consulting a filesystem symlink at all.

PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE
  - Single env var BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT pointing at the DVC cache 'md5' directory.
    - Mac dev:    /Volumes/Crucial X9/bleakhouse_audio/dvc-cache/files/md5
    - Linux dev:  /data/bleakhouse_audio/dvc-cache/files/md5  (or wherever the cache lives)
    - Fly:        /app/audio_volume/dvc-cache/files/md5
  - webapp/app.py:serve_audio rewritten to:
      1. Read run_manifest.json, find the audio_variant matching the requested filename
      2. Use variant.dvc_hash to compute path: $BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT/<hash[:2]>/<hash[2:]>
      3. Stream that file via FileResponse
      4. Symlink fallback: if hash isn't in the manifest (legacy runs without dvc_hash), fall back to the current symlink-following path
  - scripts/stage_demo.sh: drop the verbatim Mac→/app/audio_volume rewrite. Either stop staging symlinks at all (the webapp reads from BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT directly) OR keep symlinks but rewrite using the env var.
  - fly.toml / Containerfile: set BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT=/app/audio_volume/dvc-cache/files/md5 in the env block.
  - Local default: webapp falls back to /Volumes/Crucial X9/bleakhouse_audio/dvc-cache/files/md5 when the env var is unset, so existing dev setups don't break on day one.

IMPLEMENTATION ORDER (one commit each)
  1. Add BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT default + the resolution helper. webapp/app.py:serve_audio uses it.
  2. Update fly.toml to set BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT explicitly, so Fly stops relying on the symlink rewrite.
  3. Drop the stage_demo.sh symlink rewrite once Fly proves it doesn't need symlinks.
  4. Optional: drop the symlinks entirely from data/runs/*/audio/ (they become useless once the webapp resolves via hash — the symlinks are a 3.9 GB cosmetic that takes space in git status output).

MIGRATION RUNBOOK (Mac → Linux)
  1. On Mac:  tar -cf bleakhouse_audio.tar -C /Volumes/Crucial\ X9/bleakhouse_audio dvc-cache
  2. scp / rsync the tarball to the Linux box
  3. On Linux: tar -xf bleakhouse_audio.tar -C /data/bleakhouse_audio
  4. export BLEAKHOUSE_AUDIO_ROOT=/data/bleakhouse_audio/dvc-cache/files/md5
  5. uv sync && uv run uvicorn webapp.app:app --port 8000
  6. Smoke test: curl /audio/bh_trn_literary_hostprep/podcast.mp3 returns 206 + audio/mpeg

NEXT-LEVEL FOLLOW-UPS (out of scope here)
  - Move audio to S3/R2 with signed URLs — same env var pattern, different backend resolver.
  - DVC pull instead of carrying the cache around — works fine with this architecture, the env var still points at the DVC cache root.

title: /script-versions page renders empty — versioned runs archived, regex matches nothing
description: The /script-versions page (and its JSON source /tracker/versions) returns versions={} and runs=[] on the current DB state. title: Qwen-render audio variant breaks /player — manifest_qwen.json has wrong schema
description: Clicking the 'qwen' pill in the /player version switcher produces an empty transcript and a JS console error: 'TypeError: manifest.experts is not iterable' at static/player.js:235. The endpoint /api/runs/{run_id}/manifest?version=qwen returns the audio-render output schema (run_dir, refs_dir, model_id, episode_wav, episode_audio_seconds, totals, missing_speakers) instead of the script-shaped manifest the player expects (run_id, title, experts[], segments[].turns[], passages, axes, host_prep). Affects all 4 BH transport runs that have a qwen render: bh_trn_alternatives_hostprep, bh_trn_interdisciplinary_hostprep, bh_trn_literary, bh_trn_literary_hostprep. The trevelyan_v2 variant works correctly because its manifest_trevelyan_v2.json was written in the script-shaped schema. Same script underlies all renders — only the audio engine changes — so the player should keep the script structure constant and only swap the audio path.
acceptance_criteria: (a) clicking qwen on /player loads transcript with correct turn count, (b) audio src points at podcast_qwen.mp3, (c) other variants (classic, trevelyan_v2) unaffected.
notes:
Two reasonable fixes:

OPTION A (data fix): regenerate manifest_qwen.json so it carries the script structure. The Qwen rendering script (scripts/render_qwen_remote.sh + companion python) currently dumps audio-render telemetry; have it write a script-shaped manifest with a side-pocket of audio metadata, mirroring how manifest_trevelyan_v2.json is structured. Backfill the 4 existing manifest_qwen.json files.

OPTION B (player fix): in webapp/app.py:get_manifest, detect when the requested-version manifest is missing script fields (no 'experts' key) and fall back to the classic manifest, then overlay the audio_file path so the player swaps audio engines without touching the transcript. Cleaner because the script never differs across renders.

Recommend OPTION B — it's ~10 lines server-side and immune to future audio engines that emit their own telemetry. No data backfill required.
close_reason: Server-side fallback in get_manifest: when audio_manifest exists but lacks 'experts', overlay onto run-level manifest.json. Verified qwen pill click on bh_trn_literary_hostprep renders all 137 turns; classic and trevelyan_v2 unchanged.

title: Curated 'best version per (novel × panel)' listening view with cards + teasers
description:
The engineering matrix at /tracker is honest about uncertainty: 270 cells per generator, four generators, three pipelines, with-and-without hostprep, with-and-without reference tools. Most of those cells exist to answer research questions (does transport help? does hostprep help? do references change quality?) and the matrix doesn't pick a winner. For a listener who just wants to hear 'the Bleak House interdisciplinary panel', the matrix is overwhelming.

Build a curated listening view that applies opinionated defaults — those that we have some confidence in — and surfaces ONE recommended version per (novel, panel) coordinate. Defaults: audio rendered, pipeline=transport, hostprep ON, ref_tools ON, generator=anthropic_sonnet_4_6 (default). That collapses 270 cells × 4 generators down to ~45 cards (15 novels × 3 panels), and most listeners will only ever want one of those.
design: Out-of-scope on first pass: per-cell quality scoring (we don't have a single defensible metric yet). Out-of-scope: showing alternates ('see also: same novel without hostprep'). Both are easy to add once tier 1 lands.
notes:
Two implementation tiers:

TIER 1 (mechanical): a /listen or /podcasts page that runs the SQL filter (pipeline='trn' AND hostprep=1 AND ref_tools=1 AND has_audio AND generator=DEFAULT), groups by novel, and renders one card per (novel, panel) with: panel name, expert chips, audio play button, link to /report, link to /script, link to /prep. Mostly DB query + template work, leaning on existing /script-versions card styling.

TIER 2 (curated): each card carries a teaser quote (1-2 sentence pull from the episode that hooks the listener) and a 'reasons to listen' line (1-2 bullets explaining what makes this episode distinctive). Sources for the teaser:
  • Pre-computed at script-gen time (cheap, deterministic, but requires a backfill)
  • Or extracted on-demand by an LLM call, cached on disk per run
Sources for 'reasons to listen':
  • Synthesised from the chapter notes / themes already in enrichment/ data
  • Or LLM-summarised from the script with a fixed prompt (caching needed)
The teaser-extraction prompt is the interesting design question: it has to find a quote that's witty, self-contained, and gives away enough flavour without spoiling. Would draw from existing literary-element schema work (KeyMoments, ThemesAndAnalysis).

The opinionated defaults map to research observations:
 • transport > embedding > no-passages on most quote-verification metrics (per existing analysis in research.html)
 • hostprep increases turn-balance and Q/seg
 • ref_tools is 'nice' (Christopher's word) — adds reading lists without obvious script-level harm
 • anthropic default vs cerebras: still under investigation, default is the most-rendered

If/when one of these defaults flips (e.g., a future analysis shows embedding is better for some panels), the view's selection rule changes in one place rather than refactoring users' mental models around the matrix.

Naming: 'Listen' or 'Podcasts' as a top-nav item, distinct from 'Player' (which is the engineering audio player keyed off the matrix). 'Player' could even retire in favour of this if the curated view fully covers the audio-listening use case.
close_reason: Tier 1 (curated card grid at /script-versions) and tier 2 (LLM-derived teaser per card via webapp/build_teasers.py) both shipped. 22 cards across 14 novels render with full panel + experts + teaser quote + reading list + listen/report/prep links. Teasers cached on disk per run; CLI rebuilds when scripts change.

title: Tracker DVC-stale signal: collapse per-cell flags into a global banner
description: The ⚠ DVC-stale badge on /tracker cells is faithful to dvc status but useless per-cell because staleness is a global property of the codebase, not of individual runs. Audit 2026-04-30 found 1,389 of ~1,400 stale-stage triggers come from a handful of shared pipeline source files (run_pipeline.py, generate_podcast.py, podcast_types.py, host_prep.py, generate_run_manifest.py, reference_tools.py); only ~10 triggers are per-run (config.json edits). When pipeline code is touched, 194/216 runs go red simultaneously, destroying the discriminative value of the per-cell signal. Per-cell decoration assumes staleness is a per-run property; in this codebase it isn't.
acceptance_criteria: (a) decision recorded between option 1 and 2; (b) implementation matches; (c) when 100+ runs are stale only from shared code, the page doesn't decorate every cell.
notes:
Two design options on the table (Christopher's framing: 'design makes sense if staleness is uncommon'):

OPTION 1 (minimal): Drop per-cell ⚠. Add a single banner at the top of /tracker: '180 of 216 runs are stale because pipeline code changed: <list paths>. dvc repro would re-execute them.' One signal, no painting cells red.

OPTION 2 (richer): Per-cell ⚠ only when staleness is run-specific (own config.json edited, own out drifted). Hide ⚠ when the only stale reasons are shared-code paths. Add the global banner alongside so shared-code staleness is still visible. Catches 'this single run was hand-edited' as a distinct signal.

Code site: webapp/app.py:_dvc_stale_runs (l.979) returns {run_id: [phases]}; webapp/app.py:_build_tracker_matrix_from_db assigns to summary['dvc_stale_phases']; the inline JS at app.py:1626 paints the ⚠. The dvc-status JSON includes per-stage 'changed deps' / 'changed outs' fields with file paths, so option 2 is doable: classify each path as 'data/runs/<run_id>/...' (run-specific) vs other (shared).
close_reason: Moot. Issue planned to collapse per-cell DVC-stale flags into a global tracker banner. With DVC fully removed in BleakHouse-zmlw, there is no stale signal to collapse. The stale flag column was dropped entirely in BleakHouse-8tqd. Superseded by the full DVC removal.

title: Interdisciplinary sub-table doesn't filter by generator — multi-generator runs collide
description: The /tracker page's 'Interdisciplinary Panel' sub-table (#inter-table) shows the wrong q/r/w values when multiple generators have produced runs at the same (novel, pipeline). _build_tracker_matrix_from_db includes every interdisciplinary row from db_rows regardless of generator (webapp/app.py:1107-1124). The JS renderer (renderInterdisciplinary in app.py:1652) keys by byNovel[key][cond] where cond is derived from run_id — so multiple runs at the same coordinate overwrite each other and whichever happens last in SQL row order wins. Concrete instance: bh_trn_interdisciplinary_hostprep cell currently displays q=7.6 (the cerebras_zai_glm run) instead of q=5.1 (the bh_trn_interdisciplinary_hostprep_retrofit run for the default anthropic generator). Same shape as the panel-scripts bug fixed in BleakHouse-ejn (commit 254c51a).
acceptance_criteria: (a) inter_runs in app.py filtered to default generator, (b) verify in browser that bh transport-interdisciplinary cell shows q=5.1 not q=7.6, (c) Hester transport cell still shows q=6.9 (only one run, unchanged), (d) Passage to India cells unchanged.
notes: Fix follows the same pattern as panel_scripts: filter inter_runs to r['generator'] == axes.DEFAULT_GENERATOR. Alternative would be to add a per-generator dropdown to the sub-table, but the table lacks the visual room and the main matrix already handles per-generator display. Stick with default generator for the sub-table and let the main matrix carry generator-comparison work.
close_reason: Filtered inter_runs to axes.DEFAULT_GENERATOR. Verified: bh transport-interdisciplinary cell now shows q=5.1 (anthropic retrofit) not q=7.6 (zai_glm). Other cells unchanged.

title: Full new-novel run from Gutenberg, fully cost-instrumented
description:
End-to-end smoke test of the full BleakHouse pipeline on a brand-new novel (one we haven't done yet). Two purposes:

1. Confirm the new-novel onboarding path still works end-to-end after the correct-by-construction-citations refactor.
2. Get real cost numbers for every stage, not just phase 2.5 + 3.

What needs to happen:

  - Pick a Gutenberg novel we don't already have. Reasonable candidates:
    Hardy 'The Mayor of Casterbridge', Eliot 'Adam Bede', Trollope
    'The Way We Live Now', Collins 'The Moonstone', Thackeray 'Vanity
    Fair'. Smaller is faster.
  - Add it to data/novels/<key>/ and enrichment/novel_prompts.py
    (follow the pattern of an existing novel like cranford or hester).
  - Build clusters_literary.json and clusters_characters.json before the
    transport pipeline (per the run_pipeline.py memory).
  - Run the full pipeline: enrichment/run_pipeline.py with all phases
    (no --resume-from), --pipeline transport, --host-prep,
    --reference-tools, --replace-expert for the alternatives panel.

What needs instrumentation:

  - Phases 0–2 (enrichment) currently have no timing file. Need to
    extend the Recorder approach (enrichment/timing.py) to wrap the
    LLM calls in:
      enrichment/run.py  (phase 1: per-passage literary analysis)
      enrichment/run_pipeline.py  (phase 2: plan + assignments)
      Possibly phase 0 if it makes any model calls.
  - Phase 3 (enrichment/generate_podcast.py) also lacks structured
    timing. Wrap its Sonnet calls similarly. Right now we can scrape
    "input_tokens=N, output_tokens=N" from the log but a proper
    phase3_timings.json would let scripts/timings_summary.py roll up
    the whole pipeline.
  - Add a top-level run_timings.json (or extend an existing manifest)
    that aggregates every stage's events with stage labels, so a
    single timings_summary call can show enrichment vs hostprep vs
    script costs in one breakdown.

Definition of done:

  - Reading list (phase2_5_reading_list.json) + episode (phase3_episode.json)
    produced for the new novel.
  - run_timings.json rolls up every stage's events with stage labels.
  - scripts/timings_summary.py shows per-stage cost for a full run.
  - Total $ cost for a full-from-scratch run is known empirically,
    not estimated.

Reference: cranford retrofit on the new code (post-refactor) cost ~$2.70
for phase 2.5 + phase 3 only (skipped enrichment via resume-from). A
full new-novel run from scratch should add the enrichment cost on top.
acceptance_criteria: (a) reading list (phase2_5_reading_list.json) + episode (phase3_episode.json) produced for A Room with a View; (b) audio rendered as per-turn shards via render_episode_to_shards: shards.json + audio/shards/classic/ populated, every shard md5'd in the manifest; (c) shards pushed to R2 via dvc, each reachable at https://pub-<acct>.r2.dev/files/md5/<hh>/<rest>; (d) playback works end-to-end on bleakhouse-demo.fly.dev/player?run=room_with_a_view_<panel>_<config> with no text-audio drift (player advances on shard ended events, never on ms math); (e) run_timings.json rolls up every stage's events with stage labels — phases 0, 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4_audio; (f) scripts/timings_summary.py shows per-stage cost for the full run; (g) total $ cost for a full-from-scratch run is known empirically (single number, not estimate).

title: Hybrid TTS routing: dispatch accent-distinctive personas to Gemini, accent-permissive to Qwen
description: Per docs/superpowers/notes/2026-04-28-hybrid-tts-pipeline.md and the Edinburgh paper (arXiv:2601.19786), Qwen3-TTS-12Hz uses Mimi/WavLM tokens that architecturally discard accent. Confirmed empirically on Blackstone: strongly Scottish Gemini source → RP Qwen output across all ref strategies. Implement per-persona engine routing in the renderer: Blackstone (Edinburgh) and Woodcourt (Bristol) go to Gemini; Host + Cambridge + American panel personas stay on Qwen + designed ref. The render system already has per-speaker voice configs in enrichment/tts_profiles/classic.py — wire those to dispatch. Verify the seven non-Blackstone personas individually before routing them through Qwen by default.

title: Designed reference clips per persona (data/voice_refs/v1/)
description: Replace per-run extract_refs.py with frozen, prosodically-designed reference clips per persona under data/voice_refs/v1/<persona>/ref.wav. Cover prosodic slots (opener, question, em-dash beat, synthesis, sign-off, etc.) by stitching ~6-8 hand-curated clean clips from our F0-filtered pool. Pipeline reads the canonical ref instead of extracting per-job; ref version is part of the job hash so v1->v2 invalidates correctly. Solves the accent-drift problem at the source (per-run refs are inconsistent + always opener-shaped) without the fine-tuning complexity.

description: Replace per-utterance zero-shot voice cloning (Qwen3-TTS x_vector_only_mode) with a per-speaker fine-tune that locks in accent and timbre. description: Hygiene items called out in docs/synthesis_redesign.md and docs/webapp_dvc_architecture.md. (1) Cache-bust static assets — append ?v=<git-short-sha> query to <script src> and <link href> tags in webapp/templates so browser/Playwright reliably reload after a deploy. Compute SHA at app start (subprocess git rev-parse --short HEAD or read from env). Saves an hour-class of debugging when CSS/JS doesn't update. (2) Rename /versions → /script-versions (and the topbar link) — the word 'version' is overloaded between script-name-suffix versions (v1.0/v1.1) and synthesis variants (classic/qwen), and that overload caused the qwen visibility bug. (3) Internal-link audit across blog pages — the recent transparency-blog 'next post' edit pointed somewhere; spot-check every blog/* page for stale or wrong-target links. ~1–2 hours total. Reduces friction for everything downstream.

title: Replace ssh+python wrapper with REST service on pop-os for Qwen renders
description: Today's wrapper holds an ssh session open for the full 2h render and breaks on every flap (host sleep, mDNS blip, wifi). Replace with a FastAPI service on pop-os.local that owns the GPU. Endpoints: POST /render (multipart phase3 + ref audio, idempotent by hash), GET /job/<id>, GET /job/<id>/result.{wav,json}, DELETE /job/<id>. State persisted to sqlite, service runs under systemd so it restarts cleanly. Local wrapper becomes a thin HTTP client. Mirrors the fly admin upload pattern (token-gated, transient retries). Closes the recurring 'render orphaned, gpu busy on retry' problem.

title: render_qwen_remote.sh: run remote python under nohup/screen/tmux + poll for completion
description: Current wrapper holds the ssh session open for the full ~2h GPU render. If the ssh drops (network blip, host sleep, Mac wifi flap), the python keeps running on pop-os but our wrapper exits and we lose the output. Fix: run remote python under nohup/setsid/tmux so it's session-independent; the wrapper polls every N seconds for the PID to exit, then pulls. Today's interdisciplinary render hit this twice; manual workaround was a wait-and-pull script in /tmp.

title: Phase 3 prompt produces Host-light scripts without hostprep
description:
Measured over all 194 canonical runs: scripts generated WITHOUT the Phase 2.5 host-brief have dramatically weaker Host facilitation than those WITH it.

With hostprep (103 runs):
  - avg 20.95 interior Host turns per episode
  - avg 19.10 of those contain an explicit '?'
  - 0 episodes with zero interior Host turns

Without hostprep (91 runs):
  - avg 1.80 interior Host turns per episode (~12x fewer)
  - avg 0.74 with '?' (~26x fewer)
  - 27 of 91 episodes (30%) have ZERO interior Host turns
    — script is Host-intro → experts bouncing → Host-outro, with no
    Host cueing between expert turns at all

By pipeline (non-hostprep):
  emb  14/30 zero-interior (47%)
  trn   8/30 zero-interior (27%)
  nop   5/29 zero-interior (17%)

Root cause: the SYSTEM_PROMPT in enrichment/generate_podcast.py assumes
hostprep is the main driver of Host engagement. Without host_brief the
extra HOST PREPARATION block at ~l.303 isn't added, and the bare system
prompt's 'the host opens and closes each segment, steering the
conversation' is too weak — LLM just writes an intro-plus-ping-pong.

Impact: non-hostprep episodes are structurally different from hostprep.
Audio renders of these sound Host-light relative to the hostprep version;
any apples-to-apples comparison (e.g. Qwen vs Gemini TTS) should match
hostprep on both sides. Surfaced during BleakHouse-2bz Qwen TTS
experiment.

Fix options (not yet implemented):
 1. Strengthen SYSTEM_PROMPT to explicitly require the Host to introduce
    each new speaker with a named question, regardless of brief presence.
 2. Synthesise a lightweight host brief automatically when the full
    Phase 2.5 wasn't run.
 3. Deprecate the non-hostprep path and make hostprep default.

Affects 91 existing non-hostprep runs. Regenerating them all at ~dozens
of cents per episode is cheap but invalidates their DVC baseline
(BleakHouse-696); regenerate + dvc commit if we do it.

title: Post-hoc passage matching for ungrounded runs with confabulation assessment
description:
## Problem
No-passages runs have no passage_refs, so the webapp shows nothing when the reader clicks. The current "suggested passages" approach (theme/character keyword overlap) is weak — it finds vaguely related passages, not the ones the panelists actually (mis)quoted.

## Design: Quote-to-passage matching

A build-time step that runs after Phase 3, for each utterance marked is_quote=true (or quote_mode="reading"):

1. **Find the best matching passage.** For each quote utterance, slide a 5-word window across the quote text and search all passages in the novel's enriched corpus. Return the passage with the longest matching subsequence (not just boolean match — measure overlap length).

2. **Score match quality.** For each quote-passage pair, compute:
   - `match_ratio`: fraction of quote words that appear in a matching subsequence in the passage (0.0–1.0)
   - `match_category`: "verified" (ratio >= 0.6, genuine quote), "paraphrase" (0.3–0.6, recognisable but altered), "confabulation" (< 0.3, no real source)

3. **Attach to manifest.** Each matched passage goes into the manifest's passages dict with:
   - The passage text, chapter, characters, themes (same as grounded passages)
   - `match_ratio` and `match_category`
   - `matched_quote`: the utterance text that triggered the match
   - Link the utterance to this passage via passage_ref in the manifest

4. **Also match non-quote utterances that discuss passages.** When panelists paraphrase or discuss a passage without direct quotation, look for 3-word subsequences. Score these more leniently.

## Frontend display

The passage reveal shows match quality prominently:
- **Verified** (green badge): "This quote matches the novel text" + show the matching passage
- **Paraphrase** (amber badge): "Close paraphrase — the panelist is working from memory" + show the closest passage
- **Confabulation** (red badge): "No matching passage found — this may be invented or misremembered" + optionally show the closest passage anyway with its low score

This lets the reader see the confabulation rate in real time as they listen.

## Implementation

### New file: webapp/match_passages.py
- `find_best_passage_match(quote_text, passages) -> (passage_id, match_ratio)`
- `categorise_match(ratio) -> "verified" | "paraphrase" | "confabulation"`
- `match_all_quotes(episode, passages) -> dict[utterance_index, MatchResult]`

### Changes to webapp/build_manifest.py
- For ungrounded runs, after building the manifest, run match_passages on all quote utterances
- Populate passage_ref on matched utterances
- Add matched passages to the passages dict with quality scores

### Changes to webapp/static/player.js
- Passage reveal shows match_category badge with colour coding
- Match ratio shown as a small indicator

### Existing code to reuse
- enrichment/compute_metrics.py: fuzzy_quote_match() — extend from boolean to scored
- enrichment/compute_metrics.py: load_source_text() — but we need per-passage matching, not whole-novel matching. Use passages_enriched.json directly.

## Key insight
The enriched passages file has ~3K–7K passages per novel with full text. We search these individually (not the concatenated novel text) so we can identify which specific passage was (mis)quoted and show it to the reader.
close_reason: Implemented quote matching with 3-tier confabulation detection. BH: 51% verified, MotF: 50%. Deployed with colour-coded badges.

title: Host preparation pipeline (Phase 2.5)
description:
Add a preparatory stage between passage assignment (Phase 2) and script generation (Phase 3) where the host interviews each expert before recording, then uses that knowledge to ask targeted questions during the podcast.

## Design (from paper Section 5)

**Phase 2.5a: Pre-interviews.** For each expert–segment pair, the host (Haiku) conducts a short interview: "Given these passages, what strikes you? Where might you disagree with the other experts? Which passage would you most want to quote?" Each produces a PreInterviewResponse (key points, potential quotes, disagreement angles). Calls are parallel (~22 per run: 3 experts × 7.5 segments), ~1K Haiku tokens each.

**Phase 2.5b: Question planning.** For each segment, the host (Sonnet) synthesises all three experts' pre-interview responses and plans 3–5 questions designed to: draw out each expert's strongest take, set up productive disagreements, create cross-referencing opportunities, and target specific passages for quotation. Output is a HostBrief (planned questions, steering notes, cross-engagement targets). One Sonnet call per segment (~3K tokens each).

**Phase 3 integration.** The HostBrief is appended to the Phase 3 user message alongside passage assignments. Prompt instructs: "The host has prepared these questions—weave them naturally into conversation, not as rigid Q&A but as informed steering."

## Expected cost
Phase 2.5a: ~22K Haiku tokens/run (parallel, cheap). Phase 2.5b: ~22K Sonnet tokens/run. Total: ~44K additional tokens, 43% increase over current per-run budget but still dominated by Phase 3 script generation.

## Hypotheses
1. Question frequency increases from 1.7 to 3–5 per segment
2. Cross-expert referencing increases beyond current 61.4%
3. Reactive language markers increase
4. Quote pattern compliance maintained or improves
5. Expert identity not diluted

## Pydantic models needed
- PreInterviewResponse: key_points, potential_quotes, disagreement_angles
- HostBrief: planned_questions, steering_notes, cross_engagement_targets

## Files to create/modify
- enrichment/host_prep.py (new: Phase 2.5a + 2.5b)
- enrichment/podcast_types.py (new models)
- enrichment/generate_podcast.py (inject HostBrief into Phase 3 prompt)
- enrichment/run.py (integrate Phase 2.5 into pipeline)
notes:
## Conversational flow after a directed question

When the host asks a question directed at a specific expert, the flow should be:
1. The named expert responds first
2. Other panelists jump in naturally — agree, push back, riff, add their own angle
3. The host may steer or redirect, but doesn't need to mediate every exchange

This is a pub conversation between smart friends, not a panel at a conference. The host's questions are meant to *start* a thread, not produce a single answer. The system prompt should say something like:

"When the host directs a question at a specific expert, that expert responds first, but the other panelists should feel free to jump in — agreeing, disagreeing, building on what was said. The host's questions open a thread, not a slot for a single answer. Keep the energy informal and conversational."

This reinforces the existing "not parallel monologues" instruction but makes it concrete for the question-driven format.

title: full_episode.py: add retry-on-validation-failure when gpt-5.4 emits invalid enum values

title: Try passage_enrichment with strict=True hosting (Together) or self-hosted vLLM guided_json
description:
Follow-up to BleakHouse-qn0g. The Tier M-Haiku benchmark found:
- Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo on DeepInfra: 0% schema validity (returned markdown-wrapped JSON with wrong field names, e.g. 'interest' not 'interest_score').
- Qwen 2.5-72B on DeepInfra: 67% schema validity; one chapter timed out at 30 min.

Both ran with response_format={'type':'json_schema','json_schema':{...,'strict':False}} because the capabilities table marks DeepInfra strict=False (conservative default).

Two retries worth trying before declaring open-weight unviable for passage_enrichment:

1. Same models on **Together AI** (capabilities table marks Together strict=True). Same fixture; same seam; just change the hosting. If strict-enforcement is the difference, we'll see schema-validity rise.

2. Self-hosted **Modal+vLLM with guided_json** (vLLM's grammar-based constrained decoding is more reliable than provider-level response_format for complex schemas).

EXPECTED ANNUAL COST IMPACT IF SUCCESSFUL: passage_enrichment is ~50-100M tokens/year. Moving from Anthropic Batch Haiku (0-150/year) to Qwen 2.5-72B on Together would be ~0-40/year. Marginal absolute saving; bigger structural win is the API-independence story.

ALTERNATIVE APPROACH: split each chapter in half before sending (15-25 paragraphs per request instead of 30-50). The production pipeline already does this for chapters >200 paragraphs; lowering the threshold to ~25-50 might help open-weight candidates produce reliable structured output.

title: Plan revision: batching for LLM requests is desirable but not essential
description:
User policy clarification 2026-05-11: batch execution for LLM-backed pipeline jobs (passage_enrichment, passage_contexts) is desirable for cost reduction but not essential. The migration must not block on finding open-weight batch equivalents.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE PLAN

Phase 3 ('Deal with batch execution explicitly') currently treats portable batch as a load-bearing capability that must exist before passage_enrichment can flip default. Soften:
- Anthropic-native batch path stays available (opt-in).
- Portable execution path is just 'sequential or bounded-concurrency one-shots over the same logical request set'. No promise of matching Anthropic Batch economics.
- Concurrency speedups are desirable but not gating.
- Rate-limit handling (SDK retries with backoff) is the same defensive mechanism as the rest of the seam — not a new abstraction.

Implication for cost telemetry (BleakHouse-ft71):
- Anthropic Batch is now the canonical 50%-off path for volume Anthropic work; record execution_mode in the manifest so the cost difference is visible, but don't try to match that economics on the open-weight side.
- Open-weight cost lives in per-token (hosted) or per-GPU-second (self-hosted) regimes; no batch discount concept.

Implication for model survey (BleakHouse-o3ir):
- 'Batch API equivalent or absence' moves from 'important to evaluate' to 'good-to-note'.
- A candidate without a batch API is not disqualified; it just means volume tasks pay per-request rates.

Implication for Phase 4 (BleakHouse-wh0d):
- passage_enrichment and passage_contexts can flip default to open-weight on the basis of quality + cost alone; no requirement to wait until 'we have a portable batch story comparable to Anthropic Batch.'

Decision: Anthropic remains opt-in for volume tasks where its Batch discount makes it economically preferable, on a per-task basis. The seam supports this naturally because routing is per-task.

This is doc-only — update Phase 3 framing in docs/bleakhouse_anthropic_optionality_migration_plan.md when revisions land.
notes:
Scope clarification 2026-05-11: this ticket is part of the model-choice enterprise (BleakHouse-o3ir + 9k9n + 0rtg + r7g8), not an independent batch-architecture decision.

The 'batch is desirable not essential' policy informs:
- o3ir column treatment: 'batch API equivalent or absence' becomes informational (good-to-note), not gating.
- wh0d phase ordering: passage_enrichment and passage_contexts can flip default to open-weight without a portable-batch-story prerequisite.
- ft71 cost telemetry: open-weight tasks may run as per-request (no batch discount); record execution_mode in manifest so the cost difference is visible per-task per-provider.

Revisability: this policy can flip back if a survey-shortlisted provider turns out to offer batch economics that materially change the cost picture (e.g. Together adds a batch API at a steep discount). Don't treat 'batch is desirable not essential' as a fixed invariant — re-evaluate after o3ir's Stage 2 results come in.
close_reason: Plan revised: batch-is-desirable-not-essential encoded in Principle 4. Anthropic-native Batch API stays available for the 50%-off volume discount. Portable batch is just bounded-concurrency one-shots; no obligation to match Anthropic Batch economics. passage_enrichment and passage_contexts default-flips do NOT wait on a portable-batch story. Phase 6 (native vs portable batch split) is non-gating; exists so manifests record execution_mode.

title: Plan revision: define quality floor per task before default-flip
description:
If open-weight becomes the default per task, the default-flip cannot be on faith. Each task needs an explicit pass criterion.

DRAFT QUALITY FLOORS

Structured filtering / selection tasks (listener_pick, reading_list_winnow, reference_tools winnow):
- Schema validity: 100%. No JSON parse failures.
- Set overlap with Anthropic-Haiku baseline: ≥85% Jaccard on a 20-input fixture (i.e. on average, ≥4-of-5 picks agree).
- Manual spot-check: 5 fixtures hand-reviewed for 'would a reader notice the difference'.

Structured intermediate generation (design_segments, host_prep brief, passage_enrichment):
- Schema validity: 100%.
- Field-presence match: ≥95% on a 10-input fixture (no missing required fields where baseline filled them).
- Content fidelity: rubric-based comparison on 10 inputs — 'is the generated content as good as the baseline, sample-by-sample'. Requires human review.

Quote verification (quote_verification):
- Exact-match recall: ≥98% against a held-out set where the baseline got it right.
- False-positive rate: ≤2% (admit a quote the baseline rejected, where the baseline was correct).

Agentic tool-use (host_prep pre-interview):
- Tool-call validity: 100%.
- Convergence rate: agent reaches a final answer ≥98% of the time on a fixture.

Prose generation (generate_podcast):
- Schema validity: 100% (structured output for segment/turn fields).
- Blinded preference vs Anthropic baseline: ≥45% on 10 episode samples (i.e. open-weight not statistically worse). Audible content.
- Defer migration until other tasks are flipped and the human-comparison protocol exists.

ACCEPTANCE

A task's default does not flip to open-weight until:
1. A fixture exists for it.
2. The candidate model passes the floor for that task.
3. The floor + measurement is recorded in the manifest for that task's default flip.

This formalizes 'we know the new default is at least as good as the old one' instead of asserting it.

Strengthens BleakHouse-ipr3 (move eval fixtures forward).
notes:
Primary prose-tier goal is short podcasts, not long (user clarification 2026-05-11; 'a whole hour of this stuff is sometimes a bit much').

Refine the prose-generation quality floor accordingly:
- Target output: --length short (~30 min audio, ~600 words/segment per enrichment/run_pipeline.py).
- Baseline for blinded preference: Sonnet 4.6 on the short prompt (not the long prompt). Existing short runs: bh_trn_literary_hostprep_short, wh_trn_literary_short. Expand the comparison set if needed.
- Floor: ≥45% blinded preference for the candidate vs. Sonnet-on-short. 'Not statistically worse' on shorts, not 'matches the hour-long script.'

This is a meaningful shift: the migration isn't trying to preserve the current long-podcast output with an open-weight model. It's trying to produce good shorts with one. Sonnet stays available as opt-in if/when long output is desired, but the default direction is shorts.
Scope clarification 2026-05-11: this ticket is part of the model-choice enterprise (BleakHouse-o3ir + 9k9n + 0rtg + r7g8). The quality floors written here are STARTING POSITIONS, not invariants.

Revisability: floor levels are calibrated against the Anthropic baseline as currently understood. Once o3ir's Stage 2 results come in, expect changes:
- A candidate may pass the 'easy' floors trivially → tighten them.
- A candidate may fail by a small margin on prose but be unbeatable on cost → consider a 'good enough' tier below the formal floor for tasks where cost matters more than quality.
- A new candidate not yet on the shortlist may appear (open-source moves fast) → re-run the survey rather than treating the table as final.

Treat this ticket as the spec for the floor protocol (how we measure, what we measure against), not as the spec for the floor values. Values get revised as the survey reveals real numbers.

Also: the prose-tier floor specifically (>=45% blinded preference vs Sonnet-on-short) is a guess at where 'not statistically worse' lands for a small fixture. Once we have actual preference data from 3-4 candidates, the threshold may move — or be replaced by a different metric (e.g., percentage of episodes a human listener completes without stopping).
close_reason: Plan revised: quality-floor PROTOCOL encoded in Phase 2 (per-task-class floor protocols + starting values table). Floor values are starting positions, not invariants — revisable once Stage 2 of the o3ir survey produces real data. Protocol stays fixed; values learn. Prose-tier floor specifically targets short-podcast format (≥45% blinded preference vs Sonnet-on-short, not Sonnet-on-long).

description:
