Default lean: open-weight. But some tasks (script generation in particular) might keep Anthropic default by policy because audible quality is the deliverable. That's a per-task decision, not a global one.

Deliverable: a table in the plan doc with one row per task from docs/llm_call_sites.md:

| task | suggested default | rationale | overridable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| listener_pick | open-weight (small) | structured filtering; tiny prompt; sz5m validated structurally | yes |
| reading_list_winnow | open-weight (small) | same shape as listener_pick | yes |
| passage_enrichment (batch) | open-weight (mid)? | volume task; cost-sensitive | yes — Anthropic Batch discount may still win |
| passage_contexts (batch) | open-weight (mid)? | same | yes |
| quote_verification | open-weight (small) | strict structured | yes |
| design_segments | ??? | structured intermediate | yes |
| host_prep agentic loop | ??? | tool-use loop — capability-dependent | yes |
| host_prep brief | ??? | mid-length structured | yes |
| generate_podcast | Anthropic (Sonnet 4.6)? | final prose, audible | yes |
| embedding_podcast curation | ??? | mid-length structured | yes |
| reference_tools winnow | open-weight (small) | structured filtering | yes |
| test_single | (script — uses default for passage_enrichment) | sanity check; should follow the real default | yes |

This depends on the model-exploration ticket (open-weight model selection + hosting plan). Filling in the suggested-default column is the output of this ticket once exploration concludes.
notes:
Per-task routing constraint (2026-05-11): the final per-task default table must include at least one task whose default is a non-API (self-hosted) option — not every task, but at least one. This guarantees the project carries forward a deployable self-hosted path rather than ending up fully dependent on hosted APIs.

Candidates for the non-API default:
- prose generation (generate_podcast): if a 26B-70B class open-weight model on Runpod / Modal / GKE clears the prose floor, this is the natural choice — high control, good fine-tune story, no per-token API cost at sustained volume.
- passage_enrichment (batch): high volume, cost-sensitive; self-hosted vLLM eliminates per-token cost.

Tasks where a hosted-API default is fine if it scores best:
- listener_pick / reading_list_winnow / reference_tools winnow: small structured, low volume; latency + ops simplicity matter more than self-hosting independence.

This constraint affects the routing decision table's final shape: aim for a mix, not 'everything routes to hosted-API X'.

title: Plan revision: explicit per-provider structured-output capability matrix
description:
The plan hand-waves the structured-output translation:
  'when json_schema is present, translate to Anthropic output_config'
  'pass response_format={"type": "json_schema", ...} if the endpoint supports it'

These are not symmetric. Concrete mismatches the seam needs to handle:

Anthropic:
- messages.create + output_config={'format': {'type': 'json_schema', 'schema': ...}}  (newer)
- messages.parse + Pydantic model (SDK-typed; different return shape)
- tool_use pattern with a single tool whose schema = the output (older idiom)

OpenAI:
- response_format={'type': 'json_schema', 'json_schema': {'name': str, 'schema': dict, 'strict': bool}}
- The 'name' field is required.
- 'strict': true changes semantics (rejects extra properties, requires all required fields). Some endpoints implement this and some don't.

vLLM (OpenAI-compatible but with extensions):
- extra_body={'guided_json': schema} or extra_body={'guided_regex': ...} or extra_body={'guided_choice': [...]}.
- The OpenAI response_format path also works but only on recent versions.

SGLang / TGI / Ollama:
- Each implements 'OpenAI-compatible' to different degrees. JSON-schema constrained decoding is hit-and-miss.

Cerebras:
- response_format works for json_schema as of late 2025 but the 'strict' flag behaviour differs.

Revision: the seam should expose a per-provider capability flag (e.g. ProviderCapabilities.json_schema_constrained: bool, ProviderCapabilities.json_schema_strict: bool). When a task requests structured output and the configured provider lacks the capability, fail loudly at configuration time (not at first request). Add a small capabilities table to providers/__init__.py.

Also: the seam should normalize the Anthropic messages.create vs messages.parse return-shape difference so call sites don't have to know which API the provider used internally.
close_reason: Plan revised: per-provider structured-output capability matrix encoded in the 'Structured-output capability matrix' subsection of the Target Structure section, plus ProviderCapabilities type in the types sketch. Includes Anthropic messages.create vs messages.parse, OpenAI strict semantics, vLLM guided_json, SGLang grammar, Cerebras response_format quirks, TGI/Ollama partial compatibility. Phase 3 fails loudly at configuration time when a configured provider lacks a required capability.

title: Plan revision: reconcile with existing llm + llm-cerebras + cerebras-cloud-sdk deps
description:
The plan proposes a new enrichment/llm/ package and explicitly says 'do not start with LiteLLM unless there is a demonstrated need.'

But pyproject.toml already has:
- llm>=0.30 (Simon Willison's LLM CLI/library; plugin-based provider abstraction)
- llm-cerebras>=0.1.8 (LLM plugin for Cerebras)
- cerebras-cloud-sdk>=1.67.0 (direct Cerebras SDK)

And there's an experiments/cerebras/ directory (pricing.py) referenced in docs/llm_call_sites.md.

These deps must have been added for a reason. The plan dismisses LiteLLM without engaging with what's actually in the codebase — and 'llm' (the package) is a real provider abstraction we're already paying the dep cost for.

Revision: before introducing enrichment/llm/, the plan should answer:
- What was the intent behind adding the llm + llm-cerebras + cerebras-cloud-sdk deps?
- Is there pre-existing Cerebras experiment code that constitutes a partial implementation of this migration?
- Should the new seam use the llm package as its underlying provider abstraction, or build alongside?
- If neither: remove the deps in a cleanup ticket before the migration begins, so the dependency graph reflects intent.

Don't parallel-track a new abstraction without acknowledging the one that's already in the tree.
close_reason: Plan revised: reconciliation with existing llm/llm-cerebras/cerebras-cloud-sdk deps deferred to Phase 7 (Documentation and cleanup) with an explicit decision required — either commit to using the llm package underneath the seam, or remove the deps. Phase 1 introduces enrichment/llm/ without taking a dependency on llm; the survey will inform which way to resolve.

title: Plan revision: cost-per-task-per-provider as a first-class manifest field
description:
The plan mentions 'token usage where available' as a Phase 5 metric. That's too late and too soft for the project's actual motivation.

Why this matters for BleakHouse specifically:
- Anthropic Batch API is 50% off for the batch endpoints (submit_passages_enriched, submit_passage_contexts). For multi-thousand-passage runs this is the dominant cost.
- A portable batch runner against the same endpoints loses that discount; against an OpenAI-compatible Runpod-hosted open-weight model it's a completely different cost curve.
- Without per-task cost telemetry recorded at the manifest level, 'is this substitution worth it' becomes a guess.

Revision: from Phase 1 onward (not Phase 5), the ResolverResult-equivalent for LLM calls — and the per-run manifest — should record:
- provider
- model
- input_tokens (from response metadata where available)
- output_tokens
- estimated_cost_usd (computed from a small per-model price table maintained alongside the seam)
- execution_mode (one_shot | native_batch | portable_batch)

This makes 'switch listener-pick from Haiku to Llama-3-70B-via-Runpod' a quantifiable decision rather than a vibes-based one.

The price table is brittle (vendors change prices) but trivially small. Keep it as a Python dict, not a config file. Update by hand when prices change; print a warning when a model isn't in the table.
notes:
Re-scoped after user policy decision 2026-05-11.

Anthropic-Batch-discount concern recedes (Batch is now the opt-in path, not the default). The new cost concern is open-weight infra:
- Runpod / Modal GPU-second billing for self-hosted vLLM endpoints.
- Per-token pricing at hosted providers (Together, Fireworks, Cerebras, etc.).
- Idle-time cost for self-hosted (GKE node pools running between bursts).

Per-task cost telemetry is still important — arguably more so, because the cost structure now depends on hosting choice AND model choice AND volume in a way that's not obvious from the prompt size alone.

Manifest fields:
- provider
- model
- input_tokens, output_tokens
- estimated_cost_usd (from a small per-model price table)
- execution_mode (one_shot | native_batch | portable_batch)
- hosting (cerebras | runpod | modal | gke | together | fireworks | anthropic | ...)
close_reason: Plan revised: cost-per-task-per-provider as first-class manifest field, encoded in Principle 5 ('Configuration is explicit and auditable'). Manifest fields: provider, model, hosting, input_tokens, output_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, execution_mode. enrichment/llm/cost_table.py module owns the per-model price dict.

title: Plan revision: move evaluation fixtures forward — ship them with each migration, not after all migrations
description:
The plan defers evaluation harness to Phase 5, AFTER all Phase 4 migrations. That means each Phase 4 migration claims 'no regression' on faith — there's no way to check whether swapping providers degraded output until everything is done.

Revision: each Phase 4 task migration must ship with a small fixture-based regression check: fixed input(s), expected schema validity, expected behaviour. The fixture is allowed to be tiny (5-20 inputs); the point is to detect 'this provider gives valid JSON but wrong content' from day one.

For prose generation (design_segments, generate_podcast), schema validity is not enough; the plan correctly says this. Defer those tasks until Phase 5 has a real human-preference comparison mechanism. But for structured-filtering tasks (listener-pick, reading-list winnowing), a fixture comparing token-overlap or set-membership of picks against a Sonnet/Haiku baseline is enough to flag regression.

Concrete: add a 'Phase 1.5' or 'Phase 4 prerequisite' section that says 'each migrated task ships with a regression fixture; tasks without one cannot be migrated past Phase 4.'
notes:
Strengthened by user policy decision 2026-05-11: open-weight as default makes evaluation harness load-bearing, not optional.

Phase ordering implication: eval harness must exist BEFORE any task's default flips. New rough phase order under the open-weight-as-default policy:

  1. Seam (one-shot only) — current Phase 1.
  2. Evaluation harness with fixtures — moved up from Phase 5.
  3. OpenAI-compatible provider + structured-output capability matrix (BleakHouse-5b7m).
  4. Per-task default routing decisions (BleakHouse-9k9n).
  5. Per-task default flips, each gated on its fixture passing the quality floor (BleakHouse-0rtg).
  6. Native vs portable batch split — lower urgency since Anthropic is opt-in.

Without this rearrangement, the open-weight default ships on faith.
close_reason: Plan revised to move evaluation harness from old Phase 5 to new Phase 2 — load-bearing under the open-weight-default policy. Each task's default flip in Phase 5 is gated on its fixture passing the quality floor. Encoded in the revised plan.

title: Plan revision: reorder Phase 4 — listener-pick + reference_tools first, prose generation last
description:
The plan suggests Phase 4 migration order: 'quote verification → simple filtering → passage enrichment → reading-list/listener-pick → script generation last'. Based on the actual call-site shapes and recent work, a better order is:

1. host_prep listener-pick + reference_tools reading-list winnowing — Haiku-only, structurally tiny, well-validated by BleakHouse-sz5m (just rewinnowed 222 reading lists), runs on small inputs. Lowest risk; immediately useful as a provider-substitution testbed.
2. submit_passage_contexts / collect_passage_contexts — already structured around a batch boundary; clean place to introduce the portable batch runner from Phase 3.
3. submit_passages_enriched / collect_passages_enriched — the canonical Anthropic Batch job; biggest cost/quality lever; forces the native-vs-portable batch split to be real.
4. design_segments + generate_podcast + embedding_podcast — Sonnet-class prose generation, audible-quality concern, swap only after the evaluation harness exists.

test_single.py is the right place to INTRODUCE the seam (Phase 1 minimal first PR), but it's a script, not a pipeline call site. Don't conflate 'introduce the seam' with 'migrate something user-visible.'

Revision: update Phase 4's suggested order section. Add a note that test_single.py migration in Phase 1 is seam-introduction, not user-visible migration.
notes:
Re-scoped after user policy decision 2026-05-11: open-weight is the default for most tasks, Anthropic is opt-in.

The 'migration order' framing changes: rather than 'add opt-in support per task', it's 'flip the default per task'. Each flip requires:
1. A regression fixture exists (BleakHouse-ipr3).
2. The task passes its quality floor (BleakHouse-0rtg).
3. The per-task default decision is made (BleakHouse-9k9n).
4. The model+hosting choice for that task is in place (BleakHouse-o3ir).

Some tasks may NOT flip — e.g. generate_podcast (final prose) may keep Anthropic Sonnet 4.6 as default by policy because audible quality is the deliverable. That's an output of the per-task routing ticket (9k9n).

Order remains the same in spirit (small structured tasks first, prose last), but each step is now a 'flip the default' operation, not an 'add opt-in alternative' operation.

title: Re-run listener-pick LLM winnower across 222 reading lists post-jcsr
description:
After BleakHouse-jcsr completes (existing reading lists re-enriched with ISBN+DOI, reverified through the cascade with new ISBN-trust admission), the consumer-facing 'recommended[]' short list in each phase2_5_reading_list.json is still chosen by the simple top-up logic in scripts/verify_reading_list_urls.py — which preserves the original LLM picks where they still resolve, then fills to 5 from other resolved entries in original order. That's the wrong selection criterion now:

- Original picks were chosen pre-verification on the unfiltered candidate set; they don't reflect which URLs now point at real content (vs. soft-404 catalog stubs).
- After jcsr, many entries that previously resolved to OpenAlex landing pages now resolve via the ISBN step with head_verified=True (or trust-admit with head_verified=False). The listener-pick winnower (enrichment/host_prep.py:filter_reading_list_recommended) should re-run on the enriched+reverified entries[] to pick a fresh listener-friendly subset that reflects the new admission outcomes.

Scope:
1. One new script: scripts/rewinnow_recommended.py — for each phase2_5_reading_list.json, instantiate an Anthropic client and call filter_reading_list_recommended(client, path, novel_title, novel_author). Idempotent (writes back in place). Novel title/author lookup via enrichment/axes.py:NOVELS.
2. Atomic writes (tmp + rename) matching verify_reading_list_urls.py.
3. Restartable: skip runs whose recommended[] already reflects post-jcsr entries (e.g., by checking a written-after-timestamp or a marker field).
4. Rebuild data/content.db after.

Cost: 222 runs × 1 Haiku call × ~512 tokens ≈ negligible.

Dependency: blocks on BleakHouse-jcsr.
close_reason:
Re-ran the Haiku-driven listener-pick LLM winnower across all 222 reading lists. recommended[] now reflects post-jcsr admission outcomes (ISBN-resolved + trust-admitted entries) rather than the simple top-up that preserved the pre-verification original picks.

scripts/rewinnow_recommended.py (new):
- Per reading list: read entries[], filter to resolved-only (so we don't pick something the renderer would emit as an HTML comment), build CitationRecord objects, call _select_listener_recommendations (Haiku 4.5, 3-8 picks JSON), write back recommended[].
- Defensive shims: (1) strip non-CitationRecord keys ('raw_url' and friends added in later tickets); (2) synthesize tag + title for the 64 entries / 15 runs on the pre-7cgk legacy schema (openalex_title/raw_text instead of title); (3) accept axes.novel as either short key ('dc') or long ID ('david_copperfield') — 5 of 222 manifests use the long form.
- ThreadPoolExecutor(workers=4) — keeps under the 450k input-tokens/min Haiku rate limit; SDK max_retries=10 absorbs occasional 429 bursts.
- Atomic writes (tmp + rename). Cap on recommended[] at 10 if the LLM's fallback path returns the full candidate list.

Tests (9 new in test_rewinnow_recommended.py):
- _entry_to_record: strips unknown keys; handles minimal entry; legacy-schema fallbacks (openalex_title/openalex_authors/openalex_year/raw_text); raw_text fallback when openalex_title is empty.
- _novel_meta: reads run_manifest.json; returns title+author for short-key novel; accepts long-form ID; None for missing manifest / unknown key / corrupt JSON.

Live data:
- 217 runs winnowed cleanly in 96.6 sec (first sweep with 12 workers hit 429 rate limit; reduced to 4 workers + SDK retries and re-ran).
- 5 originally-skipped runs (long-form axes.novel) re-run after the fix.
- Recommended totals: 1081 (post-jcsr top-up) → 1166 (post-rewinnow). Median 5/run, range 1-7, 0 empty.
- 0 unresolved entries leak into recommended[] anywhere (the resolved-only pre-filter does the job).
- data/content.db rebuilt out-of-band (gitignored).

Cost: actual run was 4 workers × ~1.5 sec/call × 222 runs ≈ .50 as predicted (1.4M input + 18k output tokens at Haiku 4.5 pricing).

Tomalin spot-check on dc_emb_literary final recommended: [Charles Dickens: A Life (Tomalin) | source=isbn head=True] now appears — the whole chain (htfr OpenAlex tightening → 2qs0 ISBN cascade + Wikipedia-trust → jcsr corpus re-enrichment → sz5m fresh LLM winnow) lands the structurally correct citation in the consumer-facing list.

Reading-list pipeline arc complete (htfr → 2qs0 → jcsr → sz5m). 423 tests pass. Lint + pyright clean.

title: Tighten admission for legacy-schema entries with bare URLs (.jpg/admin/handle resolvers)
description:
After BleakHouse-htfr the OpenAlex soft-404 class is gone, but a separate class survives: legacy-schema entries (raw_text + openalex_* fields, no 'title') where the pre-5ccr pipeline embedded a URL directly in the entry. The verifier admits these via the raw_url cascade step (HEAD-200), even when the URL is:

- a .jpg / .png deep-link in an institutional repository (e.g. ualresearchonline.arts.ac.uk/id/eprint/8694/1/Engels%28Working-man%29ual.jpg)
- an admin URL (admin.research-repository.uwa.edu.au)
- a bare handle resolver (hdl.handle.net/...)
- a URN resolver (urn.kb.se/...)
- a non-canonical .de academic journal stub (www.jltonline.de)

Net: 14 entries across 13 runs (counted 2026-05-11 post-htfr).

Options to consider:
- raw_url step: reject by file extension (.jpg/.png/.gif/.tiff)
- raw_url step: reject host suffixes that we already know are catalog stubs (hdl.handle.net, urn.kb.se, *.handle.net)
- raw_url step: when entry is legacy-schema (no title, openalex_* present) and url isn't on a trusted host, fall through to OpenAlex re-search instead of admitting on HEAD
- Lightweight body content sniff (4 KB) requiring some keyword overlap with title

Lower priority than htfr — UX impact is small (entries have no human-visible title to attach to the link anyway, so the webapp may already hide them).

title: Measure whether context strings improve final podcast quality
description:
Hypothesis (not yet evidence-backed): the LLM-generated 'context' field
in passages_contextual.json improves the quality of downstream podcast
outputs (host briefs, episodes) versus passages_enriched.json with
context=None.

Experimental design (corrected):

  Within-novel comparison. For a given novel, run the script-generation
  pipeline twice — once with passages_contextual.json as input
  (context strings populated), once with the same passages but with
  the context field forced to None (e.g. by feeding passages_enriched.json,
  or by stripping context from the contextual file). Compare the two
  resulting podcast scripts on a fixed quality measure. Repeat across
  several novels for power.

  Holding novel + panel + pipeline + generator fixed isolates the
  context treatment. Cross-novel comparison would confound novel
  identity with the treatment and is not a valid design.

Open: what 'better outcome' means — quote-verification rate? expert
annotation? structured rubric on a sample of episodes? That choice
shapes the experiment; pick before running.

Surfaced 2026-05-09 during content.db scoping. Per project policy: no
unsupported claims about pipeline behaviour — measure or hedge.

title: Retrofit phase2_5_interviews for remaining 66 legacy hostprep runs
description:
Continuation of BleakHouse-us0 (now closed). 22 of 88 legacy hostprep runs
have been retrofitted; 66 remain.

## Estimate (scaled from us0's per-run estimate)

- ~66 × 4 experts × 8 segments = ~2,100 Claude Haiku interview calls
- ~66 × 8 = ~528 Claude Sonnet planning calls
- Distribution remaining is approximately:
    - 30 emb (only 1 emb retrofit done so far)
    - 30 nop (1 nop done)
    - 4 trn (most of the 22 done are trn)

## Recipe (proven on the 22 done)

1. uv run python scripts/list_retrofit_candidates.py to enumerate.
2. For each candidate, uv run python scripts/retrofit_hostprep.py <run_id>
   creates <run_id>_retrofit_<timestamp>Z/ with phases 0-2 copied and
   phase 2.5 + 3 regenerated.
3. uv run python -m enrichment.expdb scan picks up most of them.
4. git add config.json retrofit_manifest.json + dvc.lock + runs.yaml
   regen. dvc push -r r2 if any cache:true blobs were added.

## Known wrinkle

upsert_episode in enrichment/expdb/store.py keys on (novel, panel,
pipeline, hostprep, generator, ref_tools, length) — NOT label. So when
the canonical source run is already in expdb, the retrofit's episode
row collides; the new hostprep_version still attaches to the source
episode (so webapp source-URL routing serves retrofit data correctly),
but the retrofit's run_id is never recorded as an episode label.
Direct retrofit-URL lookups (rare, mostly debug paths) won't find it.
Filed as a separate fix-needs-design item if it becomes load-bearing.

## Why this issue exists
The original us0 mixed three steps: (1) onboard already-completed
retrofits, (2) scan stragglers, (3) run the remaining 66. Steps 1+2
done as of commit 15d02706. This issue covers step 3.
notes: Deferred to 2026-05-31. ~$155 estimated spend (Sonnet-dominated by phase 3 episode regen) not warranted right now. The 22 already-done retrofits cover the most-used novels (cran, bh, hest, pti) and the webapp serves their refreshed interviews via expdb routing.

title: webapp/app.py: tighten _load_json typing + migrate on_event to lifespan
description:

title: Open-weight Qwen + caching: A/B comparison + extractor support
description:
Captured from a 2026-05-02 design discussion about whether to swap Anthropic Haiku for an open-weight model on the passage-enrichment workload (enrichment/generate_contexts.py).

KEY FINDINGS

1. Cerebras (current phase 3 use):
   - Pricing for qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507: $0.60 / $1.20 per MTok
     (verified from data/runs/bh_trn_alternatives_hostprep_cerebras_qwen/phase3_generation_metrics.json)
   - HAS automatic prefix caching (128-tok blocks)
   - But cached tokens are billed at FULL rate — no cost discount, only latency
   - Cache hits visible at usage.prompt_token_details.cached_tokens (OpenAI shape)
   - Conclusion: bad fit for the chapter-as-cached-prefix pattern; fine for phase 3 where prompts don't repeat

2. Alibaba Qwen API (closest API-level analogue to Anthropic for caching):
   - Qwen-Flash: $0.05–0.25 in / $0.40–2.00 out per MTok
   - Qwen-Plus: $0.40–1.20 in / $1.20–3.60 out per MTok
   - Qwen-Max: $1.20–3.00 in / $6.00–15.00 out per MTok
   - Supports explicit cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'} — same API shape as Anthropic
   - Cache write 1.25x, cache hit 0.10x (explicit) or 0.20x (implicit)
   - Conclusion: would drop into generate_contexts.py with minimal code change

3. OpenRouter as a unified routing layer:
   - Supports both automatic top-level cache_control AND explicit per-block markers
   - Underlying providers it caches through: Anthropic (explicit), Qwen (explicit), OpenAI/DeepSeek/Gemini-2.5 (implicit)
   - Returns usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (OpenAI shape) + a cache_discount field (single $ figure, net effect of caching)
   - Provider sticky routing maximises hit rate but can pin to a pricier endpoint

PROPOSED WORK (when un-deferred)

A. Extend time_model in enrichment/timing.py to ALSO extract:
   - usage.prompt_token_details.cached_tokens (OpenAI/Cerebras shape)
   - top-level cache_discount (OpenRouter shape)
   So a CallEvent's cost is correct regardless of which provider responded.

B. Pricing.py additions:
   - Cerebras qwen-3-235b at $0.60/$1.20 (same rate cached or fresh)
   - Alibaba Qwen-Flash, Qwen-Plus, Qwen-Max with the cache multipliers

C. Optional ablation script: render the same chapter through Anthropic-Haiku, Qwen-Flash (Alibaba direct), Qwen-Plus (OpenRouter-routed). Compare:
   - Total $ for full enrichment
   - Cache hit rate
   - Output quality (manual review)
   This would be a vo7 sibling — research-grade comparison of the cost/quality frontier on the same workload.

WHY DEFERRED

vo7 (full new-novel run) needs the existing Anthropic-Haiku path to work end-to-end first. Adding extractor branches for Cerebras/OpenRouter shapes is only useful once we have a Cerebras or OpenRouter run actually going through the new instrumentation — which isn't in the current scope. Picking this up after vo7 ships and we have a baseline empirical cost number to A/B against.
notes: Live discussion captured 2026-05-02. References: Cerebras docs (https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/capabilities/prompt-caching), Alibaba Model Studio billing (https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/billing-for-model-studio + /context-cache), OpenRouter prompt-caching docs (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching). All rates verified from provider docs; this issue is the system of record for the comparison.

title: Backfill existing audio renders to shard format via forced alignment
description:
The 32 existing single-mp3 audio renders (BH + others) need to be converted to per-turn shards once the new shard-based architecture (BleakHouse-ec3n) is live. We can't trivially re-shard them by re-rendering — the text-to-audio mapping for existing mp3s only exists implicitly in the audio bytes. Use forced alignment to derive turn boundaries from the audio + script, then split the mp3 at those boundaries.

Approach:
- Input: existing podcast.mp3 + phase3_episode.json (script with utterance text)
- Tool: aeneas, whisper word-level timestamps, or Montreal Forced Aligner — pick one based on accuracy on TTS audio (not human speech; choose carefully)
- Output: one mp3 per turn, written into the shard layout the new system expects
- Validate: re-concatenating the shards produces a file identical (or near-identical with crossfade) to the original mp3
- Push shards to R2 via DVC
- Update DB to point at the new shard set

Quality bar:
- Per-turn boundary error < 100ms (perceptually inaudible drift even for speakers transitioning mid-sentence)
- Spot-check: motf_trn_alternatives — the run with known 15.7s drift in the old manifest — should playback correctly after backfill since alignment grounds boundaries in the audio bytes, not in stale metadata.
acceptance_criteria: (a) all 32 existing audio renders converted to shard format; (b) re-concatenated shards round-trip to within audible tolerance of the original mp3; (c) motf_trn_alternatives plays without drift on bleakhouse-demo; (d) old podcast.mp3 + audio/manifest.json files removed from the source-of-truth path.
notes: Blocked on BleakHouse-ec3n. Forced-alignment approach was Option D in the 2026-05-02 architecture discussion — rejected as the primary path (added dependency, alignment imperfect on stylised TTS) but right tool for migrating legacy data because the data lacks structural turn boundaries.
close_reason: Done in practice (2026-05-09 review): all 34 audio runs have audio/shards.json; the cited drift example motf_trn_alternatives is sharded; no podcast.mp3 files remain in data/runs/. The backfill happened through the shard-rendering path rather than forced-alignment splitting — outcome is the same.

title: Phase timings should ship as data, not be inferred from file mtimes
description: webapp/app.py:_phase_timings() computes Phase 2.5 / Phase 3 durations from mtime deltas across phase{0,1,2,2_5,3}*.json. This works locally because the original pipeline writes those files at meaningful timestamps. On Fly the durations all read 0 because Podman's COPY layer resets every file's mtime to image-build time, so the deltas degenerate uniformly. The /tracker histograms render as empty divs as a result. Mitigated for the 2026-04-30 deploy by adding cp -p to staging (preserves host-side mtimes through stage_demo.sh) but the COPY layer still wipes them; the histograms remain empty on Fly even after the cp -p fix.
acceptance_criteria: (a) data/runs/<run>/phase_timings.json exists for every run with sensible numbers, (b) /tracker histograms render with the same shape on Fly as on local, (c) _phase_timings() prefers the file over mtimes when present.
notes:
The right fix is to materialise phase durations as data, not infer them. Two equivalent options:

OPTION A (per-run file): write data/runs/<run>/phase_timings.json at pipeline-end with the explicit durations. _phase_timings() reads from it (falls back to mtime-derived for legacy runs that lack the file). One-shot backfill writes the file from current mtimes for all 216 existing runs. Add to stage_demo.sh's copy list.

OPTION B (in run_manifest.json): extend run_manifest.json's existing structure with a 'phase_timings' block. Same shape, no new file. Touches scripts/generate_run_manifest.py.

Recommendation: option A. Keeps phase_timings concerns separated from the run_manifest's audio-variant focus, easier to backfill incrementally, simpler to skip when the data isn't available.

Computation: durations are mtime(phase_X) − mtime(phase_X-1) where phase_X-1 is the immediate predecessor. _phase_timings() already has this logic; refactor it into a pure compute function that takes a Path and returns a dict, then a CLI wrapper writes that to phase_timings.json.
close_reason: phase_timings.json snapshotter + reader fallback shipped. Local + Fly both show 19 p25 / 186 p3 entries, matching shape. Snapshots survive Podman's COPY layer.

title: Listener-recommendation winnower returns prose instead of empty list when nothing qualifies
description: The Haiku-based winnower in host_prep.py emits a 'recommended' value containing an LLM refusal note ('I cannot recommend any of these works for…') split into multiple paragraph-shaped strings, rather than an empty array plus a separate note field. Concrete instance: data/runs/hest_trn_interdisciplinary_hostprep/phase2_5_reading_list.json has recommended[] with 8 string entries that together form a single prose refusal — verified[] still has 18 items, but the winnower's judgment is 'none of these are listener-suitable'. The webapp's /script-versions card renderer hits this and rendered 5 prose bullets per /tracker. Mitigated client-side in webapp/app.py (refusal detection by absence of year-marker + length heuristic) but the data shape itself is wrong: 'recommended' is supposed to be a list of citations, not unstructured prose.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Hester interdisciplinary reading_list.json has recommended=[] and a non-empty reason/note, (b) any other run with prose-shaped recommended[] entries gets re-winnowed and converted, (c) the /script-versions card renderer can drop the heuristic detection in favour of the explicit field.
close_reason: Normalised 16 reading lists (1 refusal-prose → winnower_note, 13 unwinnowed dict-lists → 4-6 picks, 14 already-clean). Webapp surfaces winnower_note explicitly; JS heuristic dropped. All 22 cards now show 0-6 properly-shaped citations.

title: /prep dropdown hides non-hostprep runs — bad discoverability when arriving via deep-link
description:
The /prep page's #run-select dropdown lists only the 113 runs that have phase2_5_host_briefs.json (i.e. ran with --host-prep). When a user lands on /prep?run=<some-run-without-prep> via a deep-link (e.g. from /tracker, /script-versions, or a blog post), the dropdown shows blank, the no-data message renders, and the user has no easy way to discover which runs DO have prep data — the dropdown is filtered to those, but its current selection is empty so it visually looks like 'pick one' rather than 'these are the available alternatives'.

Cosmetic/UX issue, not a defect. Improvements range from auto-selecting the first dropdown entry on no-data to enriching the dropdown to show all runs with status icons.
acceptance_criteria: (a) chosen option implemented, (b) user landing on /prep?run=<non-hostprep> can in one click see/pick a run with prep data, (c) no regression on the normal hostprep path.
notes:
Three plausible fixes:

OPTION A (smallest): when the URL run is non-hostprep, pre-select the first dropdown entry as a hint, and add a one-line 'Or pick a hostprep run from the menu above' under the no-data message.

OPTION B (richer): include all runs in the dropdown but visually mark which have hostprep (✓), which don't (—), and disable selection of the non-hostprep ones. User immediately sees the universe and what's available. Requires fetching all runs, not just hostprep ones.

OPTION C (fanciest): add 'Try one of these instead' under the no-data message that suggests 1-3 hostprep runs covering the same novel/panel as the URL run. Most discoverable but most code.
close_reason: Added one-line hint under the /prep no-data block pointing at the dropdown. Verified text appears for /prep?run=bh_trn_literary (a non-hostprep run).

title: /report pages lack top nav and back-to-tracker link — inconsistent with /script
description: The static report.html served by /report/{run_id} is self-contained: zero internal links, no site nav, no 'back to matrix' affordance. Users who land on a report (e.g. via the tracker popover's '▶ report' link) have only the browser back button to return. By contrast /script/{run_id} renders inside SCRIPT_VIEWER_HTML which DOES include a '← Back to tracker' link, and every other surface (player, prep, blog, etc.) has the full top-nav injected by webapp/static/nav.js. /report is the odd one out.
acceptance_criteria: (a) /report/{id} pages have a visible 'back to matrix' or top-nav link, (b) consistency with /script viewer's back-link, (c) older reports either rebuilt or gracefully degrade.
notes:
report.html is generated by webapp/build_report.py and bundled per-run. Two paths to fix:

OPTION A (template wrapper): change webapp/app.py:report endpoint to wrap the report content in a thin template that adds the standard nav. Requires either parsing the report's <head>/<body> or extracting just the inner content. Most consistent with other surfaces.

OPTION B (build_report fix): update build_report.py to inject a small top-bar (or just a back-link) into the generated HTML. Self-contained reports stay self-contained but get the affordance. Requires regenerating reports (or accepting that older reports lack the link until rebuilt).

Recommendation: option B. Reports are checked-in artefacts that survive run rebuilds independently; better that they carry their own navigation than depend on a server-side template wrap that might not be present in every download/share scenario.
close_reason: Added <nav class="report-nav"> with back-to-matrix + listen + host-prep links to build_report.py template; rebuilt all 216 reports. Verified via curl on bh_trn_literary_hostprep and hest_trn_alternatives.

title: Clean up dead seg.suggested_passages path in player.js
description: webapp/static/player.js:446 reads seg.suggested_passages and renders a 'related passages' handle on each segment header for ungrounded (no-passages) runs. The field is never populated: phase3_episode.json doesn't carry it, and webapp/build_manifest.py (the canonical post-phase3 manifest builder, invoked from enrichment/post_phase3.py:42) instead adds suggested passages into the top-level manifest.passages dict with a 'suggested': True flag — not as a per-segment ref list. So the JS code path at lines 445-470 never fires; the || [] fallback hides the bug. Either the producer drifted (build_manifest used to populate seg.suggested_passages and was changed) or the consumer was written speculatively.
acceptance_criteria: (a) decision recorded, (b) dead code path no longer present (either deleted or revived end-to-end), (c) suggested passages either render correctly on no-passages runs or the affordance is removed cleanly.
notes:
Three reasonable resolutions, depending on whether the 'related passages per segment' UX is wanted at all:

OPTION A (delete, smallest): drop player.js:445-470 and the suggested-handle CSS. The 'related passages' affordance disappears for no-passages runs; users still see the full passage list elsewhere if it's exposed. Smallest patch.

OPTION B (revive client-side): keep the JS but rewrite it to compute suggested refs from manifest.passages by filtering keys where p.suggested === true. No data change needed — build_manifest already tags them. Have to decide how to assign passages to segments since the 'suggested': True flag doesn't carry a segment association.

OPTION C (revive end-to-end): update webapp/build_manifest.py:find_suggested_passages to also annotate each manifest_segment with a 'suggested_passages' list of refs. The function already iterates segments — minor edit to capture the per-segment refs alongside the global suggested dict. Then player.js works as written.

Recommendation: option C if the segment-level suggestion is actually useful UX; option A otherwise. The 'related passages' handle's value depends on whether listeners actually click it — telemetry would help, but absent that, defer to design judgment.
close_reason: Removed both suggestedRefs blocks (header handle + reveal container), 32 lines. Player still loads correctly — verified 107 turns / 7 segments / 0 affordance regressions.

title: Strip HTML tags from OpenAlex display_name
description: OpenAlex returns titles with embedded HTML elements (e.g. 'CONSERVATION OF SYMPATHY INCRANFORD'). The webapp renders these escaped, so listeners see literal '...' text in reading lists. Fix: in enrichment/reference_tools.py::execute_search_openalex, run the OpenAlex display_name through a tag-stripping pass before storing in the CitationRegistry. A simple regex 're.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", title)' is enough — these aren't real markup, just stray formatting. Decode HTML entities (& etc) at the same time via html.unescape() while we're at it. Spotted on the cranford retrofit's entry [ref-40] Jill Rappoport, 'CONSERVATION OF SYMPATHY INCRANFORD'.

title: Add structure to phase 2.5b question planning
description:
Currently `enrichment/host_prep.py::plan_questions` is a single `client.messages.parse(output_format=HostBrief)` call per segment running on Sonnet. All steering — draw out the expert's strongest take, set up productive disagreement, target specific passages, keep it conversational — lives inside `_QUESTION_PLANNING_SYSTEM`. The Pydantic schema enforces shape; nothing enforces quality.

This works for now (good radio comes out) but it makes the output entirely dependent on the model's interpretation of the prompt. With more process structure we would be less at the mercy of the model and could potentially swap to Haiku.

Possible decomposition for future work:
  1. Extract candidate disagreement points from the expert pre-interviews (deterministic or cheap LLM step).
  2. Score each pair of expert positions for 'productive disagreement' potential.
  3. Compose the question set: top-K disagreements + a strongest-take per expert, mapped to specific passages.
  4. Optional critic pass: does each question name a passage, draw out a finding, leave room for cross-engagement?

Each step would be small enough to run on Haiku, and the rubric would be inspectable rather than buried in a system prompt.

Defer until the timing data tells us `plan_questions` is worth optimising. The Sonnet cost is currently ~one call per segment — small relative to phase 2.5a interviews.

title: Accent ABX screening harness for evaluating TTS candidates
description: Before any future TTS swap (XTTS-v2, GPT-SoVITS, ElevenLabs, next-gen models), measure whether the candidate's tokens preserve accent on a held-out multi-accent set. Per Zhong et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.19786) — the methodology that diagnosed our Blackstone failure. Inputs: VCTK or our own multi-accent test set (Scottish, Northern, Southern, Irish English at minimum), candidate TTS, GenAID accent embeddings (https://github.com/jzmzhong/GenAID). Output: per-accent-pair Accent ABX error rates + Accent COS-SIM + cross-accent VC quality scores. Fails fast if candidate model collapses accent. Saves us from another Blackstone-class iteration. ~1 day to build, then reusable for every future TTS evaluation.

title: hardware-path — scope Ampere+ / cloud GPU move for bf16 + flash-attn
description:
Turing (2070 Super) has no bf16 and no flash-attention path we can
reliably use for Qwen3-TTS. That forces fp32, which costs us ~3-4x
speed on this model family.

Compare three paths:

  3. API-hosted TTS with voice cloning (ElevenLabs, Azure, etc.):
     \$0.30 per 1k characters typical; predictable but priced per use.

at an assumed 100-session-per-month usage level, voice-cloning
availability, and lock-in. Does NOT have to commit to a path; the

stay on x_vector and look elsewhere for quality.

title: Real-time interactive panel — listener as fifth participant
description:

End goal: a listener joins an already-constructed podcast panel (Host + 3 experts) as a fifth participant, contributing via chat or voice. The four AI panelists respond to the listener's turn in character, in near-real-time.

Concretely this needs:
 - sub-1 s time-to-first-audible-response from listener turn-end
 - sustained > 1x real-time throughput, with headroom for interruptions
 - voice quality stable across improvised (non-script) utterances — a listener will notice the host sounding subtly different mid-conversation more than in pre-rendered episodes

 - session state that isn't phase3_episode.json-shaped (that file represents a finished batch render, not an evolving conversation)

Explicitly NOT in scope: synthesising the listener's own voice. They speak/type for themselves.

Batch comparison in BleakHouse-2bz is the baseline and the staging ground; this epic is the path from there to an actual conversational UI.

value: No unsupported claims policy: never assert things as fact without evidence. This covers literary claims (use enrichment data, not intuition), technical claims (check file sizes, read code), causal explanations (report correlations, don't invent mechanisms). Say 'I don't know' rather than guess. Post-hoc rationalisation is explicitly prohibited.

On macOS, 'podman system prune -a' does NOT actually reclaim host disk space. Podman runs in a VM and the VM disk image (~/Library/Containers/.../podman-machine-default/...) doesn't shrink even when you delete files inside it. To actually reclaim disk: 'podman machine rm -f && podman machine init && podman machine start'. Trade-off: every cached image for every project gets wiped and is re-pulled on demand.

Pipeline entry points by type: transport (ext/trn/hia/arc) uses enrichment/run.py with RunConfig; no-passages (nop) uses enrichment/no_passages_run.py with simpler config; embedding (emb) uses enrichment/embedding_run.py; enrichment/run_novel.py is the dispatcher. BLEAKHOUSE_NOVEL env var must be set for non-BH novels (e.g. mill_on_the_floss, our_mutual_friend, north_and_south, passage_to_india).

OpenAI gpt-5 family API surface differs from gpt-4o: (1) requires max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens (400 if max_tokens passed); (2) only accepts default temperature=1 (400 on temperature=0). Third-party openai-compat providers (DeepInfra, Together) still accept the old shape. Branch on base_url=None (OpenAI native) to pick the right kwargs. Probe code in scripts/structured_output_review.py:_probe_openai_compat() has the branch.

Verifying multi-provider claims: always fetch each provider's own docs before generalising — never extrapolate from one provider's behaviour to others. 2026-05-14 example: I guessed third-party openai-compat providers wouldn't support OpenAI's Responses API. User pushed back. Fetching docs confirmed DeepInfra, Together, and Cerebras all expose ONLY /v1/chat/completions; none document /v1/responses. The conclusion was right but the methodology was wrong (guessing). Always read: docs.deepinfra.com/llms.txt + chat/reasoning.md, docs.together.ai/docs + reasoning-models-guide, inference-docs.cerebras.ai/introduction. Each provider documents reasoning support differently within Chat Completions (DeepInfra: reasoning_effort top-level or extra_body; Together: reasoning={enabled}, chat_template_kwargs, or reasoning_effort per-model; Cerebras: reasoning_effort for gpt-oss).

Deploy the Fly demo with bash scripts/deploy_demo.sh. Two steps: tar -chf data-runs.tar --exclude='audio/podcast*.mp3' data/runs/ (dereferences DVC symlinks), then fly deploy --local-only --yes -a bleakhouse-demo. Container has the JSON tree baked in (~165 MB extra image size; instant cold start); audio mp3s stay in R2 and the webapp 302-redirects mp3 requests using URLs parsed from dvc.lock at startup. No runtime dvc pull (it deletes git-tracked orphans from removed stages); no Fly volume; no R2 secrets in container. Prerequisite: local DVC cache must be populated (uv run dvc pull -r r2 once after clone).

Anthropic Message Batches are atomic: processing_status flips from 'in_progress' to 'ended' when the entire batch completes. Results don't trickle in — when status flips, all succeeded results become available via results_url at once. The request_counts (succeeded/errored/processing) can update server-side during processing but the results stream is gated on the batch as a whole reaching 'ended'. Don't poll-collect individual results during in_progress; just poll the status.

Fly.io volume upload: use tar pipe (tar cf - -C /local/dir file | fly ssh console --machine ID -C 'tar xf - -C /remote/dir/') instead of fly sftp put. sftp drops connections on large files and refuses to overwrite. tar pipe streams directly, no temp file needed. Upload files individually for reliability. Must start machine first (fly machines start ID) and work from project directory for -a flag.

run_pipeline.py is the canonical pipeline entry point. It had two transport bugs fixed on 2026-03-25: (1) segment_model=None overriding design_segments default, (2) SupplementaryDemand object passed directly instead of extracting .dimension_boost dict. New novels also need clusters_literary.json AND clusters_characters.json before transport runs work.

When using standard tools (fly deploy, dvc pull, etc.), don't wrap them in bespoke verification scripts that re-do what the tool already does. Fly's healthcheck refuses to mark a deploy successful if the new machine doesn't respond — duplicating that with a local podman build + probe + post-deploy curl loop just adds 150 lines we maintain. Lean on the tool's built-in failure modes (logs, exit codes, healthchecks); add wrapping only where the tool has a known gap.

WhisperX-aligned-words → script-words merge in tools/forced_align/forced_align/align.py uses difflib.SequenceMatcher (LCS) over the whole episode, which is O(N*M) — ~225M ops for a ~15k-word episode. Acceptable for the v1 migration but quadratic. Future optimization: run LCS chunk-by-chunk (each chunk's whisperx-output words bucketed by start-time vs the chunk's known script range), then concatenate. ~1M ops × N chunks = ~15M total instead of 225M, and it parallelizes trivially across chunks.
